docs.title: TLS Certificates
docs.text: All gRPC communication between the HitStor server and agents is encrypted with TLS. This guide covers the default self-signed certificate behavior, custom certificate configuration, and certificate management for agents.

docs.title: Default Behavior: Self-Signed Certificates
docs.text:
When the server starts without explicit certificate configuration, it automatically generates a self-signed TLS certificate and private key. This provides encryption out of the box with no additional setup.

The auto-generated certificate is:

  • Created at server startup and held in memory
  • Valid for the server's hostname and local IP addresses
  • Suitable for testing and internal networks

No files are written to disk. A new certificate is generated each time the server restarts.

docs.title: Custom Certificates
docs.text: For production deployments, provide your own TLS certificate and private key.

docs.title: Using CLI Flags
docs.text:
hitstor serve \
  --repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo \
  --tls-cert /etc/hitstor/tls/server.crt \
  --tls-key /etc/hitstor/tls/server.key

docs.title: Using the Config File
docs.text:
# /etc/hitstor/config.yaml
serve_tls_cert: /etc/hitstor/tls/server.crt
serve_tls_key: /etc/hitstor/tls/server.key

The certificate file should contain the full chain (server certificate followed by any intermediate certificates). The key file must be an unencrypted PEM-encoded private key.

docs.title: File Permissions
docs.text:
Restrict access to the private key:

sudo chmod 0600 /etc/hitstor/tls/server.key
sudo chown root:root /etc/hitstor/tls/server.key

docs.title: Using Let's Encrypt
docs.text: HitStor does not integrate directly with Let's Encrypt or ACME. Generate certificates externally using a tool like certbot, then point HitStor at the resulting files.

docs.title: Example with Certbot
docs.text:
sudo certbot certonly --standalone -d backup.example.com

This creates certificate files at:

  • /etc/letsencrypt/live/backup.example.com/fullchain.pem
  • /etc/letsencrypt/live/backup.example.com/privkey.pem

Configure HitStor to use them:

# /etc/hitstor/config.yaml
serve_tls_cert: /etc/letsencrypt/live/backup.example.com/fullchain.pem
serve_tls_key: /etc/letsencrypt/live/backup.example.com/privkey.pem

docs.title: Renewal
docs.text:
Let's Encrypt certificates are valid for 90 days. After certbot renews the certificate, restart the HitStor server to load the new files:

sudo systemctl restart hitstor-server

To automate this, add a post-renewal hook:

# /etc/letsencrypt/renewal-hooks/deploy/hitstor-restart.sh
#!/bin/bash
systemctl restart hitstor-server

sudo chmod +x /etc/letsencrypt/renewal-hooks/deploy/hitstor-restart.sh

docs.title: Certificate Renewal
docs.text:
When replacing certificate files (from any CA, not just Let's Encrypt), restart the server to load the new certificate:

sudo systemctl restart hitstor-server

The server reads certificate files at startup. Changes to certificate files on disk are not detected at runtime.

docs.title: Agent CA Certificate
docs.text: When the server uses a self-signed certificate or a certificate from a private CA, agents must be configured to trust that CA. Use the agent_ca_cert configuration key on each agent to point at the CA certificate file.

docs.title: Agent Configuration
docs.text:
In the agent config file:

# /etc/hitstor/agent-config.yaml
agent_ca_cert: /etc/hitstor/tls/ca.crt

Or via environment variable:

# /etc/hitstor/agent.env
HITSTOR_AGENT_CA_CERT=/etc/hitstor/tls/ca.crt

The CA certificate file should be the PEM-encoded certificate of the authority that signed the server's certificate. For self-signed certificates, use the server certificate itself.

docs.title: Without a CA Certificate (Certificate Pinning)
docs.text:
If agent_ca_cert is not set, the agent trusts the server certificate it sees on its first connection and pins its SHA-256 fingerprint in /etc/hitstor/server-fingerprint (C:\ProgramData\HitStor\server-fingerprint on Windows). Later connections are refused if the server presents a different certificate, unless that certificate is valid for the server hostname under the system's trusted CAs, in which case the pin is updated automatically.

Run the first connection (for example hitstor-agent ping) on a trusted network. If you replace the server's self-signed certificate on purpose, delete the fingerprint file on each agent so it pins the new one.

docs.title: Distributing the CA Certificate
docs.text:
Copy the CA certificate to each agent machine:

scp /etc/hitstor/tls/ca.crt agent-host:/etc/hitstor/tls/ca.crt

Verify the agent can connect:

hitstor-agent ping

docs.title: Troubleshooting TLS
docs.text: Symptom Cause Solution certificate signed by unknown authority Agent does not trust the server CA Set agent_ca_cert on the agent peer certificate fingerprint ... does not match pinned The server certificate changed since the agent pinned it If the change was intended, delete the agent's server-fingerprint file; otherwise investigate a possible man-in-the-middle tls: bad certificate Certificate does not match hostname Ensure the certificate's SAN includes the server hostname or IP tls: private key does not match public key Mismatched cert and key files Regenerate or re-pair the certificate and key permission denied reading key file File permissions too restrictive Ensure the HitStor process user can read the key file

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Agent Management -- register agents that will connect over TLS
  • Security -- full security model including encryption and key derivation

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: This page covers common HitStor issues, their causes, and solutions. For each problem, the error message is shown as it appears in logs or terminal output.

docs.title: "repository not initialized"
docs.text:
Cause: The repository directory does not exist or has not been initialized with hitstor init.

Solution: Initialize the repository before starting the server or running backups:

hitstor init --repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo --password "REPO_PASSWORD"

If the directory exists but appears empty or corrupted, check that the path is correct and that the keys/, data/, index/, and snapshots/ subdirectories are present.

docs.title: "incorrect password"
docs.text:
Cause: The password provided does not match the password used when the repository was initialized.

Solution:

  1. Check the HITSTOR_PASSWORD environment variable:

    echo $HITSTOR_PASSWORD

  2. If using a password file (--password-file), verify the file contains the correct password with no trailing newline:

    wc -c /etc/hitstor/password.txt
cat -A /etc/hitstor/password.txt

  3. If using systemd, check the environment file:

    sudo cat /etc/hitstor/server.env

  4. Ensure there are no extra spaces, quotes, or escape characters in the password value.

docs.title: "lock repository: repository is locked"
docs.text:
Cause: Another HitStor process is currently using the repository, or a previous process terminated without releasing the lock.

Solution:

  1. Check for other running HitStor processes:

    ps aux | grep hitstor

  2. If no other process is running, the lock is stale. Remove it:

    hitstor unlock --repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo --password "REPO_PASSWORD"

  3. If using the server, ensure only one hitstor serve process runs against a given repository.

docs.title: "TLS connection error"
docs.text:
Cause: The agent cannot verify the server's TLS certificate. The most common causes are:

  1. The agent does not have the server certificate (missing --ca-cert)
  2. The certificate does not include the server IP in its SANs
  3. The server binary is an old version that generates certificates for 127.0.0.1 only

Diagnosis: Check which IPs the certificate includes:

openssl x509 -in /var/lib/hitstor/repo/server.crt -noout -text | grep -A1 "Subject Alternative Name"

If it only lists 127.0.0.1 and localhost, the certificate does not contain the server's real IP.

Solution:

  1. Make sure the server binary is up to date (hitstor version)

  2. Delete the old certificate to force regeneration:

    rm -f /var/lib/hitstor/repo/server.crt /var/lib/hitstor/repo/server.key

  3. Restart the server — it generates a new certificate with all local IPs:

    hitstor serve --repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo ...

  4. Verify that the new certificate includes the correct IP:

    openssl x509 -in /var/lib/hitstor/repo/server.crt -noout -text | grep -A1 "Subject Alternative Name"
# Expected: IP Address:192.168.x.x in the list

  5. Copy the certificate to the agent and configure it:

    scp hits@SERVER_IP:/var/lib/hitstor/repo/server.crt /etc/hitstor/server.crt
hitstor-agent --ca-cert /etc/hitstor/server.crt ping

    Or via config:

    agent_ca_cert: /etc/hitstor/server.crt

docs.title: "certificate signed by unknown authority"
docs.text:
Cause: The agent does not trust the TLS certificate presented by the server. This is common with self-signed certificates or private CAs.

Solution: Configure the agent to trust the server's certificate:

hitstor-agent --ca-cert /etc/hitstor/server.crt ping

Or permanently via config file:

# ~/.config/hitstor/config.yaml
agent_ca_cert: /etc/hitstor/server.crt

For self-signed certificates (the default), copy the server's server.crt from the repo directory. See TLS Certificates for details.

docs.title: "tls: bad certificate"
docs.text:
Cause: The server's TLS certificate does not match the hostname or IP address the agent is connecting to.

Solution: Verify the certificate's SANs include the server's IP:

openssl x509 -in /var/lib/hitstor/repo/server.crt -noout -text | grep -A1 "Subject Alternative Name"

If the IP is missing, delete the cert and restart the server to regenerate it with all current IPs.

docs.title: "tls: private key does not match public key"
docs.text:
Cause: The certificate file and key file do not correspond to each other.

Solution: Verify the files match:

openssl x509 -noout -modulus -in server.crt | md5sum
openssl rsa -noout -modulus -in server.key | md5sum

If the checksums differ, the files are mismatched. Regenerate or re-pair them.

docs.title: "connection refused"
docs.text:
Cause: The server is not running, or a firewall is blocking the port.

Solution:

  1. Verify the server is running:

    sudo systemctl status hitstor-server

  2. Check the server is listening on the expected port:

    ss -tlnp | grep 8420

  3. Verify firewall rules allow traffic on ports 8420 and 8421:

    sudo firewall-cmd --list-ports
# or
sudo ufw status

  4. If connecting across networks, ensure there are no intermediate firewalls or security groups blocking the port.

docs.title: Agent Not Appearing in Dashboard
docs.text:
Cause: The agent has not successfully connected to the server or completed a backup.

Solution:

  1. Check the agent can reach the server:

    hitstor-agent ping

  2. Verify the API key is correct in /etc/hitstor/agent.env.

  3. Check agent logs for errors:

    sudo journalctl -u hitstor-agent -n 50

  4. Ensure the agent name matches what was registered with hitstor serve agent add.

docs.title: Stale Agent Alerts
docs.text:
Cause: An agent has not completed a backup within the configured stale threshold (default: 25 hours).

Solution:

  1. Check the agent service is running:

    sudo systemctl status hitstor-agent

  2. Review agent logs for errors:

    sudo journalctl -u hitstor-agent --since "24 hours ago"

  3. Verify network connectivity between the agent and server.

  4. If the agent is intentionally offline (maintenance, decommissioned), remove it:

    hitstor serve agent remove AGENT_NAME

  5. Adjust the stale threshold if the backup schedule is less frequent than every 25 hours:

    # /etc/hitstor/config.yaml
alert_stale_threshold: 49  # hours

docs.title: "repository is locked for maintenance"
docs.text:
Cause: A check or prune operation is currently running on the repository. Only one maintenance operation can run at a time per repository.

Solution:

  1. Wait for the current operation to finish. Check the Storage page in the dashboard for operation progress.

  2. If the operation appears stuck, restart the server. The in-memory maintenance lock is released when the process exits.

  3. If you need to run a maintenance operation urgently, use the "Force" option from the dashboard, which aborts active backup sessions and acquires the lock.

docs.title: "acquire lock: ..."
docs.text:
Cause: A race condition where another maintenance request acquired the lock between the initial check and the lock attempt.

Solution: Retry the operation after the current maintenance task completes.

docs.title: Slow Backups
docs.text:
Cause: Network bandwidth limitations, disk I/O bottlenecks, or suboptimal parallelism settings.

Solution:

  1. Check the --parallel setting. The default is suitable for most systems, but adjust based on available CPU cores and disk speed:

    hitstor-agent backup --parallel 4 /data

  2. Monitor network throughput during backup:

    # On the server
iftop -i eth0 -f "port 8420"

  3. Check disk I/O on both the agent and server:

    iostat -x 1

  4. For large initial backups, consider running the first backup on the local network rather than over a WAN link.

  5. Review the backup output for deduplication statistics. Low deduplication ratios on subsequent backups may indicate data churn.

docs.title: Verifying Repository Health
docs.text:
Run a structural check:

hitstor check --repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo --password "REPO_PASSWORD"

For a thorough check that reads and decrypts every blob:

hitstor check --repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo --password "REPO_PASSWORD" --read-data

The --read-data flag significantly increases check duration but verifies that all data can be decrypted and matches its expected checksums.

docs.title: Check Output
docs.text:
A healthy repository produces:

check: no errors found

If errors are found, the output lists affected pack files or snapshots. Contact support or consult the repository recovery documentation.

docs.title: Log Analysis
docs.text: HitStor uses Go's slog package for structured JSON logging. Log entries include fields for timestamp, level, message, and contextual data.

docs.title: Viewing Logs
docs.text:
# Follow server logs
sudo journalctl -u hitstor-server -f

# Follow agent logs
sudo journalctl -u hitstor-agent -f

docs.title: Filtering with jq
docs.text:
Parse and filter structured JSON logs:

# Show only errors
sudo journalctl -u hitstor-server -o cat | jq 'select(.level == "ERROR")'

# Show backup-related messages
sudo journalctl -u hitstor-server -o cat | jq 'select(.msg | contains("backup"))'

# Show messages for a specific agent
sudo journalctl -u hitstor-server -o cat | jq 'select(.agent == "web-server-01")'

# Count errors in the last 24 hours
sudo journalctl -u hitstor-server --since "24 hours ago" -o cat | jq 'select(.level == "ERROR")' | wc -l

docs.title: Common Log Fields
docs.text: Field Description time ISO 8601 timestamp level Log level (DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR) msg Human-readable message agent Agent name (for agent-related events) snapshot Snapshot ID (for snapshot-related events) duration Operation duration (for timed operations) bytes Data size (for transfer operations) error Error message (for error-level entries)

docs.title: Getting Help
docs.text:
If the troubleshooting steps above do not resolve the issue:

  1. Collect server and agent logs covering the time of the problem.
  2. Note the HitStor version (hitstor version).
  3. Note the operating system and version.
  4. Open an issue on the HitStor repository with the collected information.

docs.title: HitStor Visual Branding
docs.text: Design system for the HitStor web dashboard and login experience. The goal is a cohesive, professional identity: navy depth + orange energy + clean light surfaces.

docs.title: Brand essence
docs.text:
• Trust & security — deep navy backgrounds, padlock isotipo, restrained typography
  • Action & warmth — orange accents on primary actions, active nav, and the stor wordmark syllable
  • Clarity — light content areas, white cards, generous spacing

docs.title: Color palette
docs.text: Token Hex / value Usage --brand-navy-deep #071018 Gradient start --navy #0b1f3a Gradient mid, headings on light cards --brand-navy-light #132d4f Gradient end --brand-text #f4f7fb Text on navy surfaces --brand-text-muted rgba(244,247,251,0.75) Secondary text on navy --brand-accent #ff7a45 stor syllable, version pill, nav active bar --primary #e8602c Buttons, metrics, bullet dots --primary-dark #cf4f1f Button hover --content-gradient #f8fafc → #f1f5f9 Login right panel, dashboard content background

docs.text:
Navy brand surface (header, sidebar, login left panel):

Ambient glow overlay (always paired with navy surfaces):

--brand-glow: radial-gradient(circle at 20% 20%, rgba(232,96,44,0.18), transparent 42%),
              radial-gradient(circle at 80% 70%, rgba(255,255,255,0.06), transparent 35%);

docs.title: Isotipo (assets/icon.png → internal/dashboard/static/icon.png)
docs.text:
• Rounded square padlock mark on dark ground
  • Use alone in compact spaces (header, sidebar, login card)
  • Border radius scales with size: 10px (sm), 12px (md), 18px (lg)
  • Always apply soft drop shadow on navy backgrounds

docs.title: Wordmark (HTML, not an image)
docs.text:
<span class="brand-wordmark">
  <span class="wm-hit">hit</span><span class="wm-stor">stor</span>
</span>
Syllable Color Weight hit --brand-text (white on navy) 800 stor --brand-accent (orange) 800

Letter-spacing: -0.04em. Prefer the HTML wordmark over logo.png in the dashboard shell for crisp rendering at any DPI.

docs.title: When to use which asset
docs.text: Context Asset Dashboard header Isotipo + HTML wordmark (once; not repeated in sidebar) Login hero panel Large isotipo + large wordmark README / external docs logo.svg / logo-dark.svg (SVG wordmark) Favicon favicon.png

docs.title: Typography
docs.text:
• UI: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif
  • Monospace (repo IDs, codes): SF Mono, Cascadia Code, Fira Code
  • Wordmark sizes: 2.75rem (login hero), 1.35rem (sidebar), 1.15rem (header)

│  Navy header — isotipo + wordmark · repo id · version   │

File Role assets/icon.png Master isotipo assets/logo.svg Light-background wordmark (external) assets/logo-dark.svg Dark-background wordmark (external) scripts/render-logos.sh Regenerate PNG exports via resvg

docs.title: Visual QA
docs.text:
# Post-login Overview + all pages
./scripts/screenshot-dashboard.sh

# Before/after branding comparison
OUTFILE=tmp/screenshots/brand-audit/overview-after.png \
  node scripts/.screenshot-runner/capture-overview.mjs

Screenshots are written to tmp/screenshots/ (gitignored).

docs.title: Dev Guide
docs.text: The HitStor Dev Guide is an internal reference for building, packaging, testing, and releasing HitStor. It also covers preparing a fresh Ubuntu server to receive a HitStor installation.

docs.title: Topics
docs.text: Guide Description Codebase Overview Architecture map, binaries, packages, and feature maturity. Dev Environment Install all prerequisite tools needed to build and package HitStor. Build & Packaging Compile binaries and produce .deb, .rpm, Windows, and Docker packages. Server Preparation Prepare an Ubuntu server before installing the HitStor .deb package. Testing Run unit tests, integration tests, linting, and code coverage. Benchmarks Reproducible backup/restore timings (optional restic comparison). Release Process Cut a release, generate all artifacts, and publish to GitHub.

docs.title: Performance benchmarks
docs.text:
HitStor ships a reproducible filesystem backup/restore harness under benchmarks/.

Use it to:

  • Compare releases (same machine, same profile)
  • Produce optional restic side-by-side numbers
  • Support published claims with raw JSON + methodology

Full detail: benchmarks/README.md in the repository.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
# From repository root
./benchmarks/run.sh --profile small

# Or via Make
make bench
make bench PROFILE=medium

Outputs: results.md and results.json in the work directory printed at the end of the run.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text: Profile Intent tiny Script smoke (~seconds) small Default laptop lab (~100 MiB logical) medium Publishable lab run (~1 GiB logical) large Server-class stress (~5 GiB logical)

docs.title: What “good” looks like for product messaging
docs.text:
HitStor is a filesystem backup product (Roadmap), so quote numbers that matter to filesystem buyers:

  1. Full backup MiB/s on local disk
  2. Incremental wall time after small change set
  3. Restore MiB/s (trust + RTO)
  4. On-disk repo size vs source (dedup effectiveness)

Always pair throughput with hardware class (CPU, RAM, NVMe vs HDD).

docs.title: Latest lab run
docs.text:
A format example (profile tiny, not for marketing) lives at benchmarks/results/sample-tiny.md.

Replace this section with a medium/large run on representative hardware:

./benchmarks/run.sh --profile medium --workdir /var/tmp/hitstor-bench
# paste results.md table below; archive results.json with the release
Tool Full backup Incremental Restore Repo size (MiB) Full MiB/s Restore MiB/s pending (publish medium/large run) — — — — — —

See also: restore verification (hitstor verify-restore) for correctness after restore.

docs.title: Build & Packaging
docs.text: This page documents every Makefile target for compiling binaries and producing distributable packages. All packaging-related configuration lives under the packaging/ directory.

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
make build                  # bin/hitstor        (linux/amd64)
make build-arm64            # bin/hitstor-arm64   (linux/arm64)
make build-windows          # bin/hitstor.exe     (windows/amd64)

docs.title: Agent
docs.text:
make agent                  # bin/hitstor-agent           (linux/amd64)
make agent-arm64            # bin/hitstor-agent-arm64      (linux/arm64)
make agent-windows          # bin/hitstor-agent.exe        (windows/amd64)
make agent-windows-arm64    # bin/hitstor-agent-arm64.exe  (windows/arm64)

docs.title: All Binaries
docs.text:
make build-all

Builds all server and agent binaries for every platform in a single command.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text:
make plugins

Builds all four plugin binaries to bin/:

Target Output make plugin-memory bin/hitstor-backend-memory make notifier-log bin/hitstor-notifier-log make hook-log bin/hitstor-hook-log make scanner-builtin bin/hitstor-scanner-builtin

docs.title: Protobuf Code Generation
docs.text:
Regenerate .pb.go and _grpc.pb.go files after modifying .proto definitions:

make proto            # All protos (backup + agent + plugin)
make proto-backup     # internal/proto/hitstor/v1/backup.proto only
make proto-agent      # internal/proto/hitstor/v1/agent.proto only
make proto-plugin     # api/proto/hitstor/plugin/v1/*.proto only

Note

Plugin protos require the -I api/proto include path for cross-file imports. This is already configured in the Makefile.

docs.title: Linux Packages (.deb / .rpm)
docs.text: Linux packages are built with nfpm using YAML configuration files in packaging/nfpm/.

docs.title: Makefile Targets
docs.text:
Target Prerequisite Output make pkg-server-deb bin/hitstor dist/hitstor_VERSION_amd64.deb make pkg-server-rpm bin/hitstor dist/hitstor-VERSION.x86_64.rpm make pkg-agent-deb bin/hitstor-agent dist/hitstor-agent_VERSION_amd64.deb make pkg-agent-rpm bin/hitstor-agent dist/hitstor-agent-VERSION.x86_64.rpm make pkg-linux (all above) All 4 Linux packages

Each target automatically builds its prerequisite binary first.

docs.title: Setting the Version
docs.text:
Pass the VERSION variable to control the package version:

make pkg-server-deb VERSION=1.2.0

If not specified, VERSION defaults to dev.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: nfpm reads a YAML config (e.g. packaging/nfpm/hitstor-server.yaml), takes the pre-built binary from bin/, and bundles it together with systemd units, configuration examples, and install scripts into a .deb or .rpm.

docs.title: Server Package Contents
docs.text:
Source Installed To Description bin/hitstor /usr/bin/hitstor Server binary packaging/systemd/hitstor-server.service /usr/lib/systemd/system/hitstor-server.service systemd unit packaging/systemd/hitstor-server.env.example /etc/hitstor/server.env.example Environment file template packaging/config/server-config.yaml.example /etc/hitstor/config.yaml.example Configuration template

Post-install script (packaging/scripts/server-postinstall.sh):

  • Creates hitstor system user and group
  • Creates /var/lib/hitstor, /var/log/hitstor, /etc/hitstor
  • Copies server.env.example to server.env if it does not exist
  • Runs systemctl daemon-reload

docs.title: Agent Package Contents
docs.text:
Source Installed To Description bin/hitstor-agent /usr/bin/hitstor-agent Agent binary packaging/systemd/hitstor-agent.service /usr/lib/systemd/system/hitstor-agent.service systemd unit packaging/systemd/hitstor-agent.timer /usr/lib/systemd/system/hitstor-agent.timer Daily backup timer packaging/systemd/hitstor-agent.env.example /etc/hitstor/agent.env.example Environment file template packaging/config/agent-config.yaml.example /etc/hitstor/agent-config.yaml.example Configuration template

Post-install script (packaging/scripts/agent-postinstall.sh):

  • Creates /etc/hitstor
  • Copies agent.env.example to agent.env if it does not exist
  • Runs systemctl daemon-reload

docs.title: nfpm Configuration Files
docs.text:
• packaging/nfpm/hitstor-server.yaml — server package definition
  • packaging/nfpm/hitstor-agent.yaml — agent package definition

Both use ${VERSION} and ${ARCH} environment variables, which are set by the Makefile at build time.

docs.title: Self-Extracting Installers (.run)
docs.text: Self-extracting .run installers bundle the binary, systemd units, configuration templates, and an interactive wizard into a single executable shell archive. The user downloads one file, runs it with sudo, and the wizard configures everything — passwords, ports, repository initialization, and service startup.

docs.title: Makefile Targets
docs.text:
Target Prerequisite Output make installer-server bin/hitstor dist/hitstor-server-VERSION-linux-amd64.run make installer-server-arm64 bin/hitstor-arm64 dist/hitstor-server-VERSION-linux-arm64.run make installer-agent bin/hitstor-agent dist/hitstor-agent-VERSION-linux-amd64.run make installer-agent-arm64 bin/hitstor-agent-arm64 dist/hitstor-agent-VERSION-linux-arm64.run make installers (server + agent amd64) Both amd64 installers 
make installer-server VERSION=1.2.0
make installer-agent VERSION=1.2.0

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
The build script (packaging/installer/build-installer.sh) assembles a .run file in four steps:

  1. Collect payload — copies the binary, systemd units, and config examples into a temp directory
  2. Create archive — compresses the payload into a tar.gz
  3. Inline libraries — replaces __INLINE_*__ markers in the .sh.in template with the contents of the corresponding lib/*.sh files
  4. Assemble — substitutes __VERSION__, then concatenates the assembled shell header and the tar.gz payload into a single file

The resulting .run file has this structure:

┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│ Shell script header             │  ← Installer logic (v2 template
│ (with inlined library code)     │     + all libraries inlined)
├─────────────────────────────────┤
│ __PAYLOAD_BELOW__               │  ← Marker line
├─────────────────────────────────┤
│ tar.gz binary payload           │  ← Binary + configs + service files
└─────────────────────────────────┘

At runtime, the shell header finds the __PAYLOAD_BELOW__ marker, extracts the tar.gz from that offset into a temp directory, and runs the installation steps.

docs.title: Installer Source Files
docs.text:
The v2 installer uses a modular architecture with shared libraries inlined at build time:

File Description packaging/installer/build-installer.sh Build script that assembles the .run file packaging/installer/server-installer-v2.sh.in Shell header template for the server installer packaging/installer/agent-installer-v2.sh.in Shell header template for the agent installer

Shared libraries in packaging/installer/lib/:

File __INLINE_*__ Marker Description lib/common.sh __INLINE_COMMON__ Flag parsing, color output, payload extraction, banner, root/systemd checks lib/wizard-server.sh __INLINE_WIZARD_SERVER__ Interactive server wizard (repo path, password, ports, TLS, dashboard password) lib/wizard-agent.sh __INLINE_WIZARD_AGENT__ Interactive agent wizard (server address, API key, backup paths) lib/verify.sh __INLINE_VERIFY__ Post-install verification (port listening, service status) lib/uninstall.sh __INLINE_UNINSTALL__ Clean removal of binaries, service files, config, data lib/upgrade.sh __INLINE_UPGRADE__ In-place upgrade with automatic rollback on failure

docs.title: Installer Flags
docs.text:
Both server and agent installers accept the same flags:

Flag Description --no-wizard Skip the interactive wizard (reads config from environment variables) --uninstall Remove all installed files, stop and disable services --version Print installer version and exit --help Show usage information

docs.title: Installer Behavior
docs.text:
The installer auto-detects the installation mode:

  1. Fresh install — if no existing binary is found, runs the interactive wizard (or --no-wizard for automation)
  2. Upgrade — if an existing binary is found at /usr/bin/hitstor or /usr/bin/hitstor-agent, runs the upgrade flow automatically
  3. Uninstall — when --uninstall is passed, removes everything (with confirmation prompt)

docs.title: Fresh Install (Wizard)
docs.text: The wizard prompts for all required configuration, writes config files, initializes the repository (server only), enables and starts the service, then verifies ports are listening.

docs.title: Fresh Install (--no-wizard)
docs.text:
For automated deployments, pass configuration via environment variables:

# Server
sudo HITSTOR_REPO=/var/lib/hitstor/repo \
     HITSTOR_PASSWORD=secret \
     ./hitstor-server-1.0.0-linux-amd64.run --no-wizard

# Agent
sudo HITSTOR_AGENT_SERVER=backup.example.com:8420 \
     HITSTOR_AGENT_API_KEY=<64-char-hex> \
     ./hitstor-agent-1.0.0-linux-amd64.run --no-wizard

docs.title: Upgrade with Rollback
docs.text:
When the installer detects an existing installation:

  1. Backs up the current binary to a temp location
  2. Stops the service
  3. Replaces the binary with the new version
  4. Starts the service
  5. Verifies the service is running
  6. On failure: automatically restores the backup binary and restarts the old version

Configuration files are never overwritten — user edits are always preserved. Example files are updated to the latest version.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
sudo ./hitstor-server-1.0.0-linux-amd64.run --uninstall

Stops and disables the service, removes the binary, systemd units, and optionally removes configuration and data directories (with confirmation).

docs.title: Server Installer Payload
docs.text:
File in Archive Installed To hitstor /usr/bin/hitstor hitstor-server.service /usr/lib/systemd/system/hitstor-server.service config.yaml.example /etc/hitstor/config.yaml.example + /etc/hitstor/config.yaml server.env.example /etc/hitstor/server.env.example + /etc/hitstor/server.env

The server installer also creates the hitstor system user/group and the /var/lib/hitstor and /var/log/hitstor directories.

docs.title: Agent Installer Payload
docs.text: File in Archive Installed To hitstor-agent /usr/bin/hitstor-agent hitstor-agent.service /usr/lib/systemd/system/hitstor-agent.service hitstor-agent.timer /usr/lib/systemd/system/hitstor-agent.timer agent-config.yaml.example /etc/hitstor/agent-config.yaml.example + /etc/hitstor/agent-config.yaml agent.env.example /etc/hitstor/agent.env.example + /etc/hitstor/agent.env

docs.title: Windows Packages (.exe Installers)
docs.text:
Windows installers are built with NSIS using scripts in packaging/nsis/.

Target Prerequisite Output make pkg-server-windows bin/hitstor.exe dist/hitstor-VERSION-windows-amd64-setup.exe make pkg-agent-windows bin/hitstor-agent.exe dist/hitstor-agent-VERSION-windows-amd64-setup.exe make pkg-windows (both above) Both Windows installers

docs.title: NSIS Scripts
docs.text:
• packaging/nsis/hitstor-server.nsi — server installer (installs to %PROGRAMFILES%\HitStor, adds to PATH, optional firewall rules and Windows Service registration; supports /S)
  • packaging/nsis/hitstor-agent.nsi — agent installer (installs to %PROGRAMFILES%\HitStor Agent, optional Windows Service registration)

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
make docker-build VERSION=1.2.0

Uses the multi-stage Dockerfile at the project root:

  1. Builder stage — golang:1.26-alpine, compiles the server binary
  2. Runtime stage — alpine:3.22, copies the binary, exposes ports 8420 (gRPC) and 8421 (dashboard)

docs.title: Save for Distribution
docs.text:
make docker-save VERSION=1.2.0

Produces dist/hitstor-VERSION-docker.tar.gz, a gzipped tarball that can be loaded with docker load.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text: Pushing a vX.Y.Z tag builds every release asset in CI and publishes the GitHub release. See Release Process.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
make docs-serve     # Local preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000/hitstor/
make docs-build     # Build to site/ (with --strict)
make docs-deploy    # Deploy to GitHub Pages

docs.title: Output Directory
docs.text:
All distributable artifacts are written to dist/. This directory is created automatically by the packaging targets and cleaned by:

make clean          # Removes bin/, dist/, and site/

docs.title: Codebase Overview
docs.text: This guide maps the HitStor repository for developers joining the project or updating documentation. It reflects the current tree, not historical README content.

docs.title: What HitStor Is
docs.text:
HitStor is an encrypted, deduplicated backup platform written in Go (CGO_ENABLED=0). It supports:

  • Local CLI backups — hitstor backup against a local, S3, or plugin repository
  • Centralized server/agent backups — thick-agent design over gRPC/TLS
  • Bare-metal restore — ReaR-based recovery media for Linux hosts
  • Embedded dashboard — monitoring, scheduling, restore

HitStor is filesystem-only (Windows and Linux). M365, Google Workspace, database, and cloud-VM/VMware backup were permanently removed in v2.0.0 — see Roadmap.

docs.title: Directory Layout
docs.text:
cmd/                          # Binaries (entry points)
  hitstor/                    # Main CLI + hitstor serve
  hitstor-agent/              # Remote backup agent
  hitstor-backend-memory/     # Example storage plugin
  hitstor-notifier-log/       # Example notifier plugin
  hitstor-hook-log/           # Example hook plugin
  hitstor-scanner-builtin/    # Built-in filesystem scanner plugin (ships with core agent)

internal/                     # Core libraries (not importable externally)
  archiver/                   # Local backup pipeline
  restorer/                   # Restore pipeline
  repository/                 # Content-addressable store
  server/                     # gRPC BackupService, sessions, multi-repo
  agent/                      # Remote backup client + AgentService
  dashboard/                  # Embedded web UI + HTTP API
  discovery/                  # LAN agent auto-discovery
  bmr/                        # Bare-metal restore (ReaR recovery media)
  sentinel/                   # Ransomware telemetry + Gemini analysis
  config/                     # YAML config + multi-repo repositories[]
  plugin/                     # HashiCorp go-plugin manager
  ...                         # chunker, crypto, retention, metrics, etc.

api/proto/hitstor/plugin/v1/  # Public plugin gRPC definitions
internal/proto/hitstor/v1/    # Server/agent backup protos (backup.proto, agent.proto)

packaging/                    # systemd, nfpm, NSIS, installers
docs/                         # MkDocs site (this documentation)
specs/                        # Feature specs (local only — gitignored, not part of the published repo)

docs.title: Binaries
docs.text:
Output Makefile target Role bin/hitstor make build CLI + serve bin/hitstor-agent make agent Remote agent bin/hitstor-backend-memory make plugin-memory Storage plugin example bin/hitstor-notifier-log make notifier-log Notifier plugin example bin/hitstor-hook-log make hook-log Hook plugin example bin/hitstor-scanner-builtin make scanner-builtin Built-in FS scanner plugin (ships with agent)

Build all plugins: make plugins

docs.title: Runtime Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph serverBox [hitstor serve]
        GRPC[gRPC :8420 BackupService]
        HTTP[HTTP :8421 Dashboard]
        GRPC --> Repo[(Repository)]
    end

    Agent[hitstor-agent daemon] -->|upload chunks| GRPC
    HTTP -->|WakeUp browse configure| AgentSvc[AgentService :8422]
    AgentSvc --- Agent

    CLI[hitstor backup] --> Repo

docs.title: Local backup flow
docs.text: hitstor backup → scan (internal/fs or scanner plugin) → FastCDC → dedup (session + SQLite cache + index) → encrypt → pack → snapshot.

docs.title: Agent backup flow
docs.text: Agent scans/chunks/compresses locally → CheckBlobs / UploadChunks over gRPC → server encrypts, packs, snapshots. Incremental detection uses previous snapshot metadata from BeginSession (no agent-side SQLite).

docs.title: Feature Maturity
docs.text:
Feature Status Notes Filesystem backup (CLI + agent) Stable Core engine Remote server + dashboard Stable gRPC + HTTP Backup jobs + scheduling Stable Cron, interval, timezone; job_type is always files Bare-metal restore In progress ReaR-based recovery media (Linux); see Roadmap Agent auto-discovery Stable Dashboard + /api/discover/* Ransomware Sentinel Stable Optional; Gemini via Settings or HITSTOR_SENTINEL_API_KEY

M365, Google Workspace, database, and cloud-VM/VMware backup — along with the workload collector plugin type that served them — were permanently removed in v2.0.0. See Roadmap.

docs.title: Source of Truth
docs.text:
When updating docs, prefer these files over README prose:

Topic File Config keys internal/config/config.go (Registry, RepoConfig) Dashboard HTTP routes internal/dashboard/dashboard.go (Handler() mux) Backup gRPC internal/proto/hitstor/v1/backup.proto Agent management gRPC internal/proto/hitstor/v1/agent.proto Plugin APIs api/proto/hitstor/plugin/v1/*.proto Makefile targets Makefile

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Test-first — table-driven tests in each package
  • Error wrapping — fmt.Errorf("package: action: %w", err)
  • Logging — log/slog
  • No utils/ — domain-specific packages only

docs.text:

  • Build & Packaging

  • gRPC API
  • Dashboard HTTP API

docs.title: Dev Environment Setup
docs.text: This page lists every tool required to build, package, test, and document HitStor from source.

docs.title: Go Toolchain
docs.text:
HitStor requires Go 1.26.10 or later.

go version
go version go1.26.10 linux/amd64

Set up your PATH and GOPATH so that binaries installed with go install are available:

export GOPATH="$HOME/gopath"
export PATH="$GOPATH/bin:$(go env GOROOT)/bin:$PATH"

Tip

Add these exports to your ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc so they persist across sessions.

docs.title: Protobuf Compiler
docs.text: Required only when modifying .proto files (gRPC protocol or plugin interfaces).

docs.title: protoc
docs.text:
Install the Protocol Buffers compiler:

sudo apt install -y protobuf-compiler
protoc --version
libprotoc 27.3

docs.title: Go Plugins
docs.text:
go install google.golang.org/protobuf/cmd/protoc-gen-go@latest
go install google.golang.org/grpc/cmd/protoc-gen-go-grpc@latest

Verify both are on your PATH:

which protoc-gen-go
/home/user/gopath/bin/protoc-gen-go

which protoc-gen-go-grpc
/home/user/gopath/bin/protoc-gen-go-grpc

docs.title: nfpm (Linux Packages)
docs.text:
nfpm builds .deb and .rpm packages from YAML configuration files.

go install github.com/goreleaser/nfpm/v2/cmd/nfpm@latest
nfpm --version

Warning

go install places the binary in $GOPATH/bin, not $(go env GOROOT)/bin. Make sure $GOPATH/bin is on your PATH.

docs.title: NSIS / makensis (Windows Packages)
docs.text:
Required only when building Windows .exe installers.

sudo apt install -y nsis
makensis -VERSION

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
Required only when building container images.

Install Docker Engine following the official documentation.

docker --version

docs.title: Documentation Tools
docs.text:
MkDocs with the Material theme generates the documentation site.

pip install mkdocs-material
mkdocs --version

This also installs all required Markdown extensions (admonitions, tabbed, superfences, etc.).

docs.text: Tool Purpose Verify go 1.26+ Compilation go version protoc Proto code generation protoc --version protoc-gen-go Go protobuf plugin which protoc-gen-go protoc-gen-go-grpc Go gRPC plugin which protoc-gen-go-grpc nfpm .deb / .rpm packaging nfpm --version makensis Windows installers makensis -VERSION docker Container builds docker --version mkdocs Documentation site mkdocs --version git Source control git --version make Build automation make --version

Referencia para mantener una terminología uniforme en la documentación, el repositorio y el dashboard de HitStor. Se trata al lector de usted.

Inglés Español Notas backup (sustantivo) respaldo "Backup job" → "tarea de respaldo" back up (verbo) respaldar "Back up a folder" → "Respaldar una carpeta" restore restauración (sust.), restaurar (verbo) snapshot instantánea La primera vez en cada página: "instantánea (snapshot)" repository / repo repositorio agent agente server servidor dashboard dashboard Se mantiene en inglés storage almacenamiento "Storage page" → "página Almacenamiento" retention policy política de retención prune depurar (verbo), depuración (sust.) docs.title: Estados en el dashboard
docs.text: Las etiquetas de estado (badges) se escriben en masculino singular, porque se comparten entre tareas, sesiones, restauraciones y agentes: completado, fallido, omitido, pendiente, en ejecución, desactivado, atrasado, inactivo, suspendido, nunca. Los valores técnicos cortos se mantienen: ok, info, cli.

docs.title: Reglas
docs.text:
• No traducir: bloques de código, comandos, flags, nombres de archivos, rutas, claves de configuración (serve_dashboard_password), variables de entorno, nombres de API ni salidas de la CLI (la CLI se mantiene en inglés).
  • Los nombres de elementos de la interfaz (botones, páginas) van en el idioma del dashboard al que se refiere el texto: en español, los nombres en español.
  • En la documentación (MkDocs), los encabezados traducidos conservan el anchor en inglés: ## Instalar { #install }. En los README de GitHub no se usa esa sintaxis: los enlaces internos apuntan al anchor del encabezado en español.

docs.title: Release Process
docs.text: Releases are built and published by GitHub Actions when a version tag is pushed.

docs.title: Cut a Release
docs.text:
git tag -a v1.2.0 -m "HitStor 1.2.0"
git push origin v1.2.0

The tag starts two workflows:

Workflow What it does .github/workflows/release.yml Runs go test ./..., then make release-assets VERSION=1.2.0, and creates the GitHub release v1.2.0 with every file in dist/ attached. Release notes are generated from the commits since the previous tag. .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml Builds the Docker image and pushes it to GHCR (ghcr.io/hooperits/hitstor) tagged 1.2.0 and 1.2.

The version embedded in the binaries and in the artifact names is the tag without the leading v.

After the workflows finish, deploy the documentation if it changed:

make docs-deploy

docs.title: Release Assets
docs.text:
make release-assets runs clean, build-all, pkg-linux, pkg-windows, the .run installers for amd64 and arm64, and checksums. For VERSION=1.2.0, dist/ contains:

dist/
├── hitstor-server-1.2.0-linux-amd64.run
├── hitstor-server-1.2.0-linux-arm64.run
├── hitstor-agent-1.2.0-linux-amd64.run
├── hitstor-agent-1.2.0-linux-arm64.run
├── hitstor_1.2.0_amd64.deb
├── hitstor-1.2.0-1.x86_64.rpm
├── hitstor-agent_1.2.0_amd64.deb
├── hitstor-agent-1.2.0-1.x86_64.rpm
├── hitstor-1.2.0-windows-amd64-setup.exe
├── hitstor-agent-1.2.0-windows-amd64-setup.exe
└── SHA256SUMS

scripts/install-agent.sh downloads hitstor-agent-VERSION-linux-ARCH.run from the latest release, so both .run architectures must be present.

docs.title: Build Locally
docs.text:
To reproduce the release assets on a workstation (requires Go, nfpm, NSIS and Python with Pillow for the Windows icon):

make release-assets VERSION=1.2.0

make release VERSION=1.2.0 builds the same assets plus the Docker image tarball (dist/hitstor-1.2.0-docker.tar.gz, requires Docker).

docs.title: VERSION Variable
docs.text:
The VERSION variable is passed to all build steps via Go linker flags (-ldflags). It controls:

  • The version string embedded in the binary (hitstor version)
  • Package version in .deb, .rpm and Windows installer metadata
  • Docker image tag (hitstor:VERSION)
  • Output file names in dist/

Two additional variables are set automatically:

Variable Source Example VERSION Makefile argument (default: dev) 1.2.0 COMMIT git rev-parse --short HEAD 9341885 DATE date -u +%Y-%m-%d 2026-02-24

docs.title: Partial Builds
