docs.title: Clean
docs.text:
Remove all build artifacts:

make clean

This deletes bin/, dist/, and site/.

docs.title: Server Preparation
docs.text:
This page covers what to do on a fresh Ubuntu server before installing HitStor. It covers OS-level prerequisites only. For post-installation steps (init, serve, systemd), see Server Setup.

Using the .run installer?

The Linux Quick Install (.run) handles user creation, directory setup, configuration, repository initialization, and service startup automatically via an interactive wizard. You only need the System Updates, Firewall, and Storage sections from this page.

docs.title: System Updates
docs.text:
Start with a fully updated system:

sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y

docs.title: Required Packages
docs.text:
Ubuntu ships with systemd by default. Install the additional packages HitStor depends on:

sudo apt install -y ca-certificates openssl
Package Purpose systemd Service management (pre-installed on Ubuntu) ca-certificates TLS certificate validation for agent connections openssl TLS certificate generation

Note

The .deb post-install script automatically creates the hitstor system user, group, and all required directories. No manual user creation is needed.

docs.title: Firewall Configuration
docs.text:
HitStor uses two TCP ports:

Port Protocol Service 8420 TCP gRPC — agent communication 8421 TCP Web dashboard and Prometheus metrics

docs.title: Install and Configure ufw
docs.text: sudo apt install ufw

docs.title: Open Both Ports
docs.text:
Warning

Always allow SSH (port 22) before running ufw enable, or you may lose remote access to the server.

sudo ufw allow 22/tcp comment "SSH"
sudo ufw allow 8420/tcp comment "HitStor gRPC"
sudo ufw allow 8421/tcp comment "HitStor Dashboard"
sudo ufw enable

Verify the rules:

sudo ufw status verbose

docs.title: Restrict Dashboard to LAN
docs.text:
If the dashboard should only be accessible from the local network:

sudo ufw allow from 10.0.0.0/24 to any port 8421 proto tcp comment "HitStor Dashboard (LAN)"

Replace 10.0.0.0/24 with your actual network range.

docs.title: Storage Considerations
docs.text:
Repository data lives at /var/lib/hitstor/repo by default.

  • Estimate storage: raw data size divided by expected deduplication ratio. Typical dedup ratios range from 2x to 10x depending on how similar the backed-up data is across snapshots.
  • Dedicated volume: mount a separate partition or volume at /var/lib/hitstor to isolate backup storage from the OS disk.
  • Filesystem: ext4 or XFS. Both work well; XFS performs slightly better with large files.
  • Permissions: the post-install script sets /var/lib/hitstor to mode 750, owned by hitstor:hitstor.
# Example: mount a dedicated volume
sudo mkfs.xfs /dev/sdb1
sudo mkdir -p /var/lib/hitstor
echo '/dev/sdb1 /var/lib/hitstor xfs defaults 0 2' | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab
sudo mount /var/lib/hitstor

docs.title: TLS Certificates
docs.text: HitStor generates an in-memory self-signed certificate on startup when no certificate is configured. This is fine for testing, but production deployments should use proper certificates.

docs.title: Self-Signed with OpenSSL
docs.text:
sudo mkdir -p /etc/hitstor/tls
sudo openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:4096 -nodes \
    -keyout /etc/hitstor/tls/server.key \
    -out /etc/hitstor/tls/server.crt \
    -days 365 -subj "/CN=HOSTNAME"
sudo chmod 600 /etc/hitstor/tls/server.key
sudo chown hitstor:hitstor /etc/hitstor/tls/server.key /etc/hitstor/tls/server.crt

Replace HOSTNAME with the server's FQDN or IP address.

docs.title: Let's Encrypt
docs.text:
sudo apt install -y certbot
sudo certbot certonly --standalone -d backup.example.com

For detailed TLS configuration, see TLS Certificates.

docs.title: .run Installer
docs.text:
The .run installer with the interactive wizard handles everything:

  1. Creates system group and user hitstor
  2. Creates directories: /var/lib/hitstor, /var/log/hitstor, /etc/hitstor
  3. Installs the binary and systemd service
  4. Writes configuration files from wizard answers (mode 600)
  5. Initializes the backup repository
  6. Enables and starts the service
  7. Verifies the service is running and ports are listening

docs.title: .deb Package
docs.text:
When you install the .deb package with dpkg -i, the post-install script handles:

  1. Creates system group hitstor (if it does not exist)
  2. Creates system user hitstor with home /var/lib/hitstor and shell /usr/sbin/nologin
  3. Creates directories: /var/lib/hitstor, /var/log/hitstor, /etc/hitstor
  4. Sets ownership to hitstor:hitstor and mode 750
  5. Copies server.env.example to server.env (mode 600) if no existing server.env
  6. Runs systemctl daemon-reload to pick up the new service file

You still need to manually edit configuration files and initialize the repository after package installation.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
1. Recommended: Install with the interactive wizard: Linux Quick Install (.run)
  2. Or install the package: Linux Packages
  3. Initialize the repository and start the server: Server Setup

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: This page covers how to run tests, check coverage, and documents known gotchas encountered during development.

docs.title: Unit Tests
docs.text:
make test

Runs go test ./... across all packages. No external dependencies or built binaries required.

docs.title: Integration Tests
docs.text:
make build agent
make test-integration

Runs go test -tags integration ./.... Integration tests require pre-built server and agent binaries.

docs.title: Linting
docs.text:
make lint

Runs go vet ./... to catch common issues.

docs.title: Code Coverage
docs.text:
Generate a coverage report and view it in the browser:

go test -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...
go tool cover -html=coverage.out

Target: 80%+ per package (achieved in feature 008).

docs.title: Known Gotchas
docs.text:
Issues encountered during development that are worth remembering:

Issue Solution go-plugin v1.7.0 GRPCClient signature First parameter must be context.Context bufconn gRPC tests fail silently on large messages Add grpc.MaxRecvMsgSize(math.MaxInt32) to dial options Proto cross-file imports fail Use -I api/proto include path (already in Makefile) Scanner plugin streaming differs from other plugins Scanner uses server-side streaming; the other 3 plugin types use unary RPCs Test breakage after scanner type refactor Use type ScanResult = scanner.ScanResult (type alias) instead of a new type

docs.title: Translations
docs.text: HitStor's web dashboard and this documentation are available in English and Spanish. Both are built so that more languages can be added without code changes. The CLI, installers and log messages stay in English.

docs.title: Choosing the language
docs.text:
The dashboard picks the language for each browser in this order:

  1. The language chosen with the selector in the header (or on the login page), stored in the hitstor_lang cookie.
  2. The server default, serve_dashboard_language in the server's config.yaml (for example es).
  3. The browser's preferred languages (Accept-Language).
  4. English.
hitstor config set serve_dashboard_language es

Restart the server after changing the default.

docs.title: How messages are stored
docs.text:
Messages are keyed by their English text. English needs no catalog, and any message without a translation is shown in English.

Each language is a directory under internal/i18n/locales/:

internal/i18n/locales/
├── en/
│   └── _meta.json
└── es/
    ├── _meta.json
    ├── common.json
    ├── login.json
    └── ...            one fragment per dashboard area

_meta.json names the language:

{"code": "es", "name": "Español", "complete": true}

Fragments map English text to the translation. Placeholders in braces must be kept:

{
  "Backups": "Respaldos",
  "{n} days ago": "hace {n} días"
}

In templates, text is marked with {{t "Backups"}} or {{tf "{n} days ago" "n" .Days}}. In JavaScript, with t('Backups') or t('{n} days ago', {n: days}).

docs.title: Adding a language
docs.text:
1. Create internal/i18n/locales/<code>/_meta.json with "complete": false (the code is the language tag browsers send, e.g. fr or pt-BR).
  2. Copy the Spanish fragments as a starting point and translate the values, keeping the English keys and the {placeholders}.

  3. Run the catalog tests:

    go test ./internal/i18n/ ./internal/dashboard/ -run 'TestCatalog|TestNegotiate'

    TestCatalogsComplete lists untranslated messages for languages marked "complete": true and, for every language, translations that are no longer used. TestCatalogPlaceholders checks the placeholders.

  4. When every message is translated, set "complete": true so the tests keep the language complete as the dashboard changes.

  5. Rebuild the server. The new language appears in the selector automatically.

docs.title: When you change dashboard text
docs.text: Every new or changed English message must be added to each complete language; TestCatalogsComplete fails until it is. Messages shown from runtime values (for example job statuses translated with {{t .Status}}) are listed one per line in internal/dashboard/i18n-dynamic/*.txt so the test knows they are used.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The site uses mkdocs-static-i18n with one file per language next to each page: quickstart.md (English) and quickstart.es.md (Spanish). A page without a translation falls back to English.

  • Keep the English anchors on translated headings so links work in every language: ## Inicio rápido { #quick-start }.
  • Keep link targets pointing to the English file names (quickstart.md#dashboard-password); the plugin maps them to the right language.
  • Menu titles for each language are set under nav_translations in mkdocs.yml.
  • Terminology for Spanish is in the Spanish glossary.

To add a documentation language, add it under the i18n plugin's languages in mkdocs.yml and create <page>.<code>.md files.

Build the site locally:

pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
make docs-build

docs.title: Repository files
docs.text: README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md and benchmarks/README.md have Spanish versions (*.es.md) linked from the first line of each file.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
HitStor provides two binaries:

  • hitstor -- the backup server, CLI tool, and web dashboard.
  • hitstor-agent -- a lightweight remote agent that sends encrypted, deduplicated backups to a HitStor server over gRPC.

Choose the installation method that best fits your environment.

New to HitStor? Start with the Quick Start guide — Docker server + agent binaries in ~15 minutes.

docs.title: Installation Methods
docs.text: Method Platforms Best For Quick Start Docker + Linux/Windows agents Fastest path: Docker server, VM installer, or agent-only Linux Quick Install (.run) Ubuntu, Debian, RHEL, Fedora, AlmaLinux Interactive wizard — configures, initializes, and starts everything. Built-in upgrade with rollback and uninstaller. Linux Packages (deb/rpm) Debian, Ubuntu, RHEL, Fedora, AlmaLinux Production servers with package manager Build from Source Any OS with Go 1.26+ Development, custom builds, unsupported architectures Windows Server Windows 10+, Windows Server 2016+ Running the HitStor server on Windows Windows Agent Windows 10+, Windows Server 2016+ Backing up Windows machines to a remote HitStor server Docker Any Docker host Containerized deployment, CI/CD pipelines

docs.title: After Installation
docs.text:
Once HitStor is installed, continue with:

  1. Getting Started -- end-to-end tutorial covering init, backup, restore, verify, and prune.
  2. Configuration -- config file schema, environment variables, and flag precedence.
  3. Command Reference -- detailed documentation for every command.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text: See Upgrading for instructions on upgrading an existing HitStor installation.

docs.title: Docker Deployment
docs.text: HitStor provides a multi-stage Dockerfile that produces a minimal Alpine-based container image. The image runs the HitStor server with gRPC and web dashboard support.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Docker 20.10+ or a compatible container runtime
  • Docker Compose v2 (for the compose-based deployment)

docs.title: Build the Image
docs.text:
From the repository root:

docker build -t hitstor:latest .

To build with a specific version tag:

docker build -t hitstor:1.0.0 \
  --build-arg VERSION=1.0.0 \
  --build-arg COMMIT=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) \
  --build-arg DATE=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d) .

Or use the Makefile target:

make docker-build VERSION=1.0.0

docs.title: Image Details
docs.text:
The Docker image uses a two-stage build:

  1. Builder stage -- golang:1.26-alpine compiles the static binary with CGO_ENABLED=0.
  2. Runtime stage -- alpine:3.22 with only ca-certificates and tzdata installed.

The image runs as a non-root hitstor user.

Property Value Base image alpine:3.22 User hitstor Exposed ports 8420 (gRPC), 8421 (dashboard) Volumes /var/lib/hitstor (data), /etc/hitstor (config) Entrypoint /entrypoint.sh Default command serve

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
For the full end-to-end guide (Docker server + agent installation), see Quick Start.

Run the server directly with Docker:

docker run -d \
  --name hitstor \
  -p 8420:8420 \
  -p 8421:8421 \
  -v hitstor-data:/var/lib/hitstor \
  -e HITSTOR_PASSWORD=my-secret-password \
  -e HITSTOR_REPO=/var/lib/hitstor/repo \
  hitstor:latest

docs.title: Quickstart (local repository)
docs.text:
For evaluation and homelab use:

cp .env.example .env
# edit HITSTOR_PASSWORD
docker compose -f docker-compose.quickstart.yml up -d

See Quick Start for agent setup and the optional MinIO (--profile s3) stack.

docs.title: Production
docs.text: The production deployment uses docker-compose.prod.yml:

docs.title: 1. Create the Configuration Directory
docs.text:
mkdir -p config

Place your config.yaml in this directory. You can copy and edit the example:

cp packaging/config/server-config.yaml.example config/config.yaml
editor config/config.yaml

docs.title: 2. Set Environment Variables
docs.text:
Create a .env file in the repository root:

HITSTOR_VERSION=latest
HITSTOR_PASSWORD=my-secret-password

Or export the variables in your shell before running docker compose.

docs.title: 3. Start the Services
docs.text: docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d

docs.title: 4. Verify
docs.text:
Check that the container is running and healthy:

docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml ps

The health check uses wget to poll the dashboard on port 8421 every 30 seconds.

View the logs:

docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml logs -f

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Port Protocol Description 8420 TCP gRPC server -- agent connections and CLI operations 8421 TCP Web dashboard

docs.title: Volumes
docs.text: Mount Point Description /var/lib/hitstor Repository data. This is where encrypted backup packs, indexes, and snapshots are stored. Use a named volume or bind mount to persistent storage. /etc/hitstor Configuration files. Mounted read-only from the host config/ directory.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Description HITSTOR_PASSWORD Repository password used for encryption and decryption. HITSTOR_REPO Path to the repository inside the container (default: /var/lib/hitstor/repo). HITSTOR_VERSION Image version tag used by docker-compose.prod.yml.

docs.title: Health Check
docs.text:
The production compose file includes a built-in health check:

healthcheck:
  test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://localhost:8421/"]
  interval: 30s
  timeout: 5s
  retries: 3

Docker reports the container as healthy once the dashboard responds on port 8421. Use docker inspect or docker compose ps to check the health status.

docs.title: Saving the Image
docs.text:
To export the image as a tarball for offline deployment:

make docker-save VERSION=1.0.0

This writes dist/hitstor-1.0.0-docker.tar.gz. Load it on the target host with:

docker load < hitstor-1.0.0-docker.tar.gz

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Getting Started -- initialize a repository and create your first backup.
  • Configuration -- full config file reference.
  • Upgrading -- how to upgrade a Docker deployment.

docs.title: Linux Quick Install
docs.text:
The fastest way to install HitStor on a Linux server. Download a single .run file, execute it, and the interactive wizard configures everything — no package manager, no build tools, no dependencies.

Requirements

  • Linux (amd64 or arm64)
  • systemd
  • Root privileges (sudo)
  • Tested on Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, RHEL 9+, Fedora 39+, AlmaLinux 9+

docs.title: Install the Server
docs.text:
Download the installer from the GitHub Releases page and run it:

wget https://github.com/hooperits/hitstor/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/hitstor-server-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run
chmod +x hitstor-server-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run
sudo ./hitstor-server-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run

The interactive wizard will prompt for:

  1. Data directory — where HitStor stores data (default: /var/lib/hitstor)
  2. Dashboard password — web UI login password (optional; if empty, the server generates one on first start — see Dashboard Password)
  3. gRPC port — for agent connections (default: 8420)
  4. Dashboard port — for the web UI (default: 8421)

After confirming, the installer creates the system user, starts the service, and verifies everything is running. Repositories are created from the dashboard after installation.

docs.title: Non-Interactive Install
docs.text:
For automation, use --no-wizard with environment variables:

sudo HITSTOR_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/hitstor \
     HITSTOR_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD=dashpass \
     HITSTOR_GRPC_PORT=8420 \
     HITSTOR_DASHBOARD_PORT=8421 \
     ./hitstor-server-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run --no-wizard

docs.title: Installed Files
docs.text: Path Description /usr/bin/hitstor Server binary /usr/lib/systemd/system/hitstor-server.service systemd service unit /etc/hitstor/config.yaml Server configuration /etc/hitstor/server.env Environment variables /var/lib/hitstor/ Data directory (default path) /var/log/hitstor/ Log directory

docs.title: Install the Agent
docs.text:
Download the agent installer and run it:

wget https://github.com/hooperits/hitstor/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/hitstor-agent-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run
chmod +x hitstor-agent-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run
sudo ./hitstor-agent-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run

The wizard offers two setup modes:

  1. Dashboard-managed (recommended) — the agent generates a token and waits for registration from the server dashboard. Prompts for listen port (default: 8422) and optional backup paths.
  2. Legacy (manual) — provide server address and API key from hitstor serve agent add <name>. Includes a connection test.

After installation, dashboard-managed agents display the agent token and instructions for adding the agent from the dashboard.

docs.title: Non-Interactive Install
docs.text:
Dashboard-managed mode (default):

sudo HITSTOR_AGENT_LISTEN_PORT=8422 \
     ./hitstor-agent-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run --no-wizard

Legacy mode (set server and API key to trigger):

sudo HITSTOR_AGENT_SERVER=backup-server.internal:8420 \
     HITSTOR_AGENT_API_KEY=your-64-char-hex-key \
     HITSTOR_AGENT_PATHS=/etc,/home \
     ./hitstor-agent-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run --no-wizard

docs.title: Installed Files
docs.text: Path Description /usr/bin/hitstor-agent Agent binary /usr/lib/systemd/system/hitstor-agent.service systemd service unit /usr/lib/systemd/system/hitstor-agent.timer Daily backup timer /etc/hitstor/agent-config.yaml Agent configuration /etc/hitstor/agent.env Environment variables (listen port, server address) /etc/hitstor/agent-token Agent token for dashboard registration (mode 0600)

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
Running the installer on an existing installation automatically detects the upgrade:

sudo ./hitstor-server-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run

The upgrade process:

  1. Displays the current and new version for confirmation
  2. Backs up the current binary to /usr/bin/hitstor.rollback
  3. Stops the service (if running)
  4. Installs the new binary and systemd units
  5. Updates example config files (your working configs are never touched)
  6. Restarts the service and verifies it is healthy
  7. On verification failure: automatically rolls back to the previous version

Use --no-wizard to skip the confirmation prompt (for automation).

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text: The v2 installer includes a built-in uninstaller:

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
sudo ./hitstor-server-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run --uninstall

This removes the binary, systemd service, configuration, logs, and system user. You will be asked separately whether to remove the data directory (/var/lib/hitstor) — default is no to protect your backups.

docs.title: Agent
docs.text:
sudo ./hitstor-agent-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run --uninstall

This removes the binary, systemd service/timer, and configuration.

docs.title: Version Check
docs.text: HitStor can check for newer versions via the GitHub Releases API.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text: hitstor version --check

docs.title: Automatic (Server)
docs.text: When update_check: true is set in /etc/hitstor/config.yaml (the default), the server checks for updates every 24 hours. If a newer version is available, a banner appears at the top of the web dashboard.

docs.title: ARM64 Support
docs.text:
ARM64 (aarch64) installers are also available. Download the arm64 variant:

sudo ./hitstor-server-X.Y.Z-linux-arm64.run
sudo ./hitstor-agent-X.Y.Z-linux-arm64.run

docs.title: Installer Flags
docs.text: Flag Description --no-wizard Non-interactive mode (reads from environment variables) --uninstall Remove HitStor and all associated files --yes Skip confirmation prompts --version Print installer version and exit --help Show help

docs.title: Permission Denied
docs.text:
The installer must be run as root:

sudo ./hitstor-server-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run

docs.title: systemd Not Found
docs.text: The .run installer requires systemd. If your system does not have systemd, use the Build from Source method and manage the process manually.

docs.title: Status 226/NAMESPACE
docs.text:
On some virtualized environments (Hyper-V VMs, containers, WSL), systemd security hardening may cause the service to fail with exit code 226. To fix this, edit the service unit and comment out the hardening directives:

sudo systemctl edit hitstor-server

Add the following overrides:

[Service]
ProtectSystem=
ProtectHome=
ProtectKernelTunables=
ProtectKernelModules=
ProtectControlGroups=
PrivateTmp=
NoNewPrivileges=

Then restart:

sudo systemctl restart hitstor-server

See Troubleshooting for more details.

docs.title: Linux Packages (deb/rpm)
docs.text:
Pre-built packages for Debian/Ubuntu (.deb) and RHEL/Fedora/AlmaLinux (.rpm) in amd64 architecture.

Prefer the .run installer for easier setup

The Linux Quick Install (.run) provides an interactive wizard that configures everything automatically — passwords, ports, repository initialization, and service startup. Packages require manual configuration (see below).

docs.title: Download
docs.text:
Download the latest packages from the GitHub Releases page. Each release includes four Linux packages:

Package Description hitstor_x.y.z_amd64.deb Server -- Debian/Ubuntu hitstor-x.y.z.x86_64.rpm Server -- RHEL/Fedora/AlmaLinux hitstor-agent_x.y.z_amd64.deb Agent -- Debian/Ubuntu hitstor-agent-x.y.z.x86_64.rpm Agent -- RHEL/Fedora/AlmaLinux

docs.title: Install the Server
docs.text:
Debian / UbuntuRHEL / Fedora 
sudo dpkg -i hitstor_x.y.z_amd64.deb

sudo rpm -i hitstor-x.y.z.x86_64.rpm

The package installs:

Path Description /usr/bin/hitstor Server binary /usr/lib/systemd/system/hitstor-server.service systemd service unit /etc/hitstor/server.env.example Environment file template /etc/hitstor/config.yaml.example Configuration file template

docs.title: Install the Agent
docs.text:
Debian / UbuntuRHEL / Fedora 
sudo dpkg -i hitstor-agent_x.y.z_amd64.deb

sudo rpm -i hitstor-agent-x.y.z.x86_64.rpm

The agent package installs:

Path Description /usr/bin/hitstor-agent Agent binary /usr/lib/systemd/system/hitstor-agent.service systemd service unit /usr/lib/systemd/system/hitstor-agent.timer systemd timer for scheduled backups /etc/hitstor/agent.env.example Environment file template /etc/hitstor/agent-config.yaml.example Configuration file template

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: After installation, create your configuration files from the provided examples.

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
sudo cp /etc/hitstor/server.env.example /etc/hitstor/server.env
sudo cp /etc/hitstor/config.yaml.example /etc/hitstor/config.yaml

Edit /etc/hitstor/server.env to set the repository path and password:

sudo editor /etc/hitstor/server.env

Edit /etc/hitstor/config.yaml to configure the server (listen address, TLS certificates, dashboard settings, etc.):

sudo editor /etc/hitstor/config.yaml

docs.title: Agent
docs.text:
sudo cp /etc/hitstor/agent.env.example /etc/hitstor/agent.env
sudo cp /etc/hitstor/agent-config.yaml.example /etc/hitstor/agent-config.yaml

Edit /etc/hitstor/agent.env to set the server address and API key:

sudo editor /etc/hitstor/agent.env

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
Enable and start the HitStor server:

sudo systemctl enable --now hitstor-server

Check the service status:

sudo systemctl status hitstor-server

View logs:

journalctl -u hitstor-server -f

docs.title: Agent
docs.text:
Enable and start the HitStor agent:

sudo systemctl enable --now hitstor-agent

To enable the timer for scheduled backups instead of running the agent continuously:

sudo systemctl enable --now hitstor-agent.timer

docs.title: Verify the Installation
docs.text:
hitstor version

This prints the version, commit hash, and build date. If the command is not found, ensure /usr/bin is in your PATH.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
Debian / UbuntuRHEL / Fedora 
sudo systemctl disable --now hitstor-server
sudo dpkg -r hitstor

sudo systemctl disable --now hitstor-server
sudo rpm -e hitstor

Configuration files in /etc/hitstor/ are preserved during removal. Delete them manually if no longer needed.

docs.title: Build from Source
docs.text: Building from source is recommended for development, testing, or when pre-built packages are not available for your platform. HitStor compiles with CGO_ENABLED=0, producing fully static binaries with no runtime dependencies.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Go 1.26+ -- HitStor uses log/slog and other features from recent Go releases.
  • git -- to clone the repository.
  • make -- to use the provided build targets (optional but recommended).

docs.title: Clone the Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/hooperits/hitstor.git
cd hitstor

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
make build

The binary is written to bin/hitstor.

docs.title: Agent
docs.text:
make agent

The binary is written to bin/hitstor-agent.

docs.title: Build Without Make
docs.text:
If you prefer to build manually:

# Server
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o bin/hitstor ./cmd/hitstor/

# Agent
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o bin/hitstor-agent ./cmd/hitstor-agent/

docs.title: Cross-Compilation
docs.text:
Because HitStor compiles with CGO_ENABLED=0, cross-compilation is straightforward. The Makefile includes targets for common platforms:

# Linux ARM64 (Raspberry Pi, AWS Graviton)
make build-arm64
make agent-arm64

# Windows amd64
make agent-windows

# Windows ARM64
make agent-windows-arm64

To cross-compile manually for any platform:

# macOS AMD64
GOOS=darwin GOARCH=amd64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o bin/hitstor-darwin-amd64 ./cmd/hitstor/

# macOS ARM64 (Apple Silicon)
GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o bin/hitstor-darwin-arm64 ./cmd/hitstor/

The resulting binary is a single static file with no external dependencies.

docs.title: Install to PATH
docs.text:
Copy the binary to a directory in your $PATH:

sudo cp bin/hitstor /usr/local/bin/
sudo cp bin/hitstor-agent /usr/local/bin/

docs.title: Verify the Build
docs.text:
hitstor version

This prints the version, commit hash, and build date. During development builds, the version is reported as dev.

You can also verify with:

hitstor --help

docs.title: Running Tests
docs.text:
To run the test suite after building:

make test

For integration tests:

make test-integration

docs.title: Build All Targets
docs.text:
To build all binaries (server, agent, and all cross-compiled variants) in a single command:

make build-all

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Getting Started -- initialize a repository and create your first backup.
  • Configuration -- set up a config file to avoid repeating flags.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Get HitStor running in about 15 minutes. This guide covers the four recommended paths for early adopters:

  1. Docker — fastest way to run the server (developers and homelab)
  2. Linux VM installer — production-style server on a single machine
  3. Windows Server installer — server as a Windows Service
  4. Agent only — connect laptops and servers to an existing HitStor server

Agents are always native binaries installed on each machine you want to back up. The server can run in Docker or on a VM.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Docker 20.10+ and Docker Compose v2
  • 2 GB RAM and a few GB of free disk for the repository volume

docs.title: 1. Configure environment
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/hooperits/hitstor.git
cd hitstor
cp .env.example .env

Edit .env and set a strong HITSTOR_PASSWORD (repository encryption) and HITSTOR_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD (web UI login). If you leave HITSTOR_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD empty, the server generates a new random dashboard password on every container start — see Dashboard Password.

docs.title: 2. Start the server
docs.text:
docker compose -f docker-compose.quickstart.yml up -d

On first start, the container automatically runs hitstor init and then hitstor serve.

docs.title: 3. Open the dashboard
docs.text:
Navigate to http://localhost:8421 and log in with HITSTOR_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD (or the generated password, see Dashboard Password).

Port Service 8421 Web dashboard 8420 gRPC (agents connect here)

docs.title: 4. Install an agent
docs.text: On each machine to back up, install the agent binary. See Path D below.

docs.title: Optional: S3 storage with MinIO
docs.text:
To store backups in S3-compatible storage instead of a local Docker volume:

docker compose -f docker-compose.quickstart.yml --profile s3 up -d

This starts HitStor with s3:http://minio:9000/hitstor-backups and a bundled MinIO instance. The MinIO console is at http://localhost:9001 (minioadmin / minioadmin).

Development only

The bundled MinIO credentials are for local testing. Do not expose this stack to the internet without changing credentials and enabling TLS.

docs.title: Pull a pre-built image
docs.text:
When release images are published to GHCR:

export HITSTOR_IMAGE=ghcr.io/hooperits/hitstor
export HITSTOR_VERSION=latest
docker compose -f docker-compose.quickstart.yml up -d

Build locally instead:

docker compose -f docker-compose.quickstart.yml build
docker compose -f docker-compose.quickstart.yml up -d

docs.title: Stop and remove
docs.text:
docker compose -f docker-compose.quickstart.yml down
# Add -v to delete repository data volumes

docs.title: Path B: Linux VM Installer
docs.text: Use this when you prefer a native server install without Docker — typical for a dedicated backup VM.

docs.title: 1. Download the server installer
docs.text:
From GitHub Releases:

wget https://github.com/hooperits/hitstor/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/hitstor-server-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run
chmod +x hitstor-server-*.run
sudo ./hitstor-server-*.run

The interactive wizard initializes the repository, configures systemd, and starts the server.

docs.title: 2. Open the dashboard
docs.text:
Default URL: https://<server-ip>:8421 (self-signed TLS) or http://<server-ip>:8421 depending on wizard settings. Log in with the dashboard password you entered in the wizard; if you left it empty, see Dashboard Password.

See Linux Quick Install for wizard details and Server Setup for production hardening.

docs.title: 3. Install agents
docs.text: Continue with Path D.

docs.title: Path C: Windows Server Installer
docs.text: Use this to run the server on Windows Server 2016+ (or Windows 10 1809+) as a Windows Service.

docs.title: 1. Run the installer
docs.text:
Download hitstor-X.Y.Z-windows-amd64-setup.exe from GitHub Releases and run it as Administrator, or install unattended from an elevated PowerShell:

.\hitstor-X.Y.Z-windows-amd64-setup.exe /S

The installer copies hitstor.exe to C:\Program Files\HitStor, creates C:\ProgramData\HitStor\config.yaml, adds firewall rules for ports 8420 and 8421, and registers and starts the HitStor service. Running a newer installer the same way upgrades in place.

docs.title: 2. Get the dashboard password
docs.text: The server generates a random dashboard password on first start. Read it on the server as described in Dashboard Password.

docs.title: 3. Open the dashboard
docs.text:
Open http://<server-ip>:8421, log in, and change the password under Settings. Then create a repository from the Storage page. Until a repository exists the server runs in setup mode and serves the dashboard over plain HTTP; HTTPS (self-signed by default) is enabled after a repository is configured and the service restarts (Restart-Service HitStor).

See Windows Server for service management and firewall details.

docs.title: 4. Install agents
docs.text: Continue with Path D.

docs.title: Path D: Agent Only
docs.text: Install hitstor-agent on every machine whose data you want in the repository.

docs.title: Linux
docs.text:
wget https://github.com/hooperits/hitstor/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/hitstor-agent-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run
chmod +x hitstor-agent-*.run
sudo ./hitstor-agent-*.run

Choose dashboard registration mode. The wizard prints an agent token. In the HitStor dashboard:

  1. Go to Agents → Add Agent
  2. Enter the token and the agent's IP address
  3. Create a backup job under Backups

For scripted installs:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hooperits/hitstor/master/scripts/install-agent.sh | sudo bash

See Agent Deployment for daemon mode, database jobs, and Windows.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text: Download hitstor-agent-X.Y.Z-windows-amd64.exe from Releases and run the installer. See Windows Agent.

docs.title: Verify connectivity
docs.text: From the agent host, the server gRPC port must be reachable (default 8420). Agents poll the server for backup schedules; you can also trigger Backup Now from the dashboard.

docs.title: Dashboard Password
docs.text:
HitStor has no default dashboard password. The password comes from:

Install path Source Docker HITSTOR_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD in .env Linux VM installer The password entered in the wizard Windows installer Generated on first start

When the config file has no dashboard password, hitstor serve generates a random one at startup, saves its hash to the config file, and writes the plaintext once to the server log, in an entry that contains no dashboard password configured; generated one. You do not need dashboard access to read it — read the log on the server.

docs.title: Read the generated password
docs.text:
Windows (PowerShell as Administrator; the log is readable only by Administrators and SYSTEM):

Select-String -Path C:\ProgramData\HitStor\logs\server.log -Pattern 'generated one' |
  Select-Object -Last 1 |
  ForEach-Object { ($_.Line | ConvertFrom-Json).fields.password }

Linux:

sudo grep 'generated one' /var/log/hitstor/server.log | tail -1
# or
sudo journalctl -u hitstor-server | grep 'generated one' | tail -1

Docker:

docker compose -f docker-compose.quickstart.yml logs hitstor | grep 'generated one' | tail -1

Copy and paste the value rather than typing it — generated passwords mix characters that look alike (l/I, O/0).

Log in and change the password under Settings right away. The log keeps the original entry, so after you change the password the logged value no longer works.

docs.title: Reset a lost password
docs.text:
Remove the stored password from the config file and restart the server; a new password is generated and logged as above.

Windows:

Stop-Service HitStor
$cfg = 'C:\ProgramData\HitStor\config.yaml'
(Get-Content $cfg) -notmatch '^serve_dashboard_password:' | Set-Content $cfg -Encoding ascii
Start-Service HitStor

Linux:

sudo sed -i '/^serve_dashboard_password:/d' /etc/hitstor/config.yaml
sudo systemctl restart hitstor-server

Docker: set a new HITSTOR_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD in .env and recreate the container (docker compose -f docker-compose.quickstart.yml up -d --force-recreate).

docs.title: First Backup Checklist
docs.text:
After server and at least one agent are connected:

  1. Storage — confirm a repository exists (Docker quickstart creates one automatically; VM wizard creates one during install)
  2. Agents — agent shows as connected in the dashboard
  3. Backups — create a job (files, database, etc.) and assign it to the agent
  4. Run — click Backup Now or wait for the schedule
  5. Restore — test a restore from the dashboard or CLI

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Getting Started — backup, restore, retention
  • Docker Deployment — production compose, image details, offline export
  • Agent Deployment — production agent setup
  • Configuration — config file reference

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text: This page covers how to upgrade an existing HitStor installation. Repositories are forward-compatible: newer versions of HitStor can read and write repositories created by older versions without any migration steps.

docs.title: Before You Upgrade
docs.text:
1. Check your current version and available updates:

    hitstor version
hitstor version --check

    Tip

    The server automatically checks for updates every 24 hours and displays a banner in the web dashboard when a newer version is available.

  2. Back up your configuration files. While upgrades preserve configuration, it is good practice to save a copy before proceeding:

    # Linux
sudo cp -r /etc/hitstor /etc/hitstor.bak

# Windows (PowerShell)
Copy-Item -Recurse "$env:ProgramData\HitStor" "$env:ProgramData\HitStor.bak"

  3. Review the release notes on the GitHub Releases page for any breaking changes or required manual steps.

docs.title: Linux Quick Install (.run)
docs.text:
Run the new .run installer on an existing installation. The installer automatically detects the upgrade, displays the version comparison, and handles the entire process:

sudo ./hitstor-server-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run

The upgrade process:

  1. Displays current and new version for confirmation
  2. Backs up the current binary
  3. Stops the service, installs the new binary and systemd units
  4. Never overwrites your working configuration files (only updates example files)
  5. Restarts the service and verifies it is healthy
  6. On verification failure: automatically rolls back to the previous version

Use --no-wizard to skip the confirmation prompt for automated upgrades.

The same process works for the agent:

sudo ./hitstor-agent-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run

docs.title: Linux Packages
docs.text:
Download the new package from GitHub Releases and install it over the existing one.

Debian / UbuntuRHEL / Fedora 
sudo dpkg -i hitstor_x.y.z_amd64.deb

sudo rpm -U hitstor-x.y.z.x86_64.rpm

The same applies to the agent package:

Debian / UbuntuRHEL / Fedora 
sudo dpkg -i hitstor-agent_x.y.z_amd64.deb

sudo rpm -U hitstor-agent-x.y.z.x86_64.rpm

Restart the services after upgrading:

sudo systemctl restart hitstor-server
sudo systemctl restart hitstor-agent

Verify the new version:

hitstor version

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
Rebuild the image and restart the container:

# Pull latest source (if building from source)
git pull

# Rebuild the image
docker build -t hitstor:latest .

# Restart with the new image
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml down
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d

Or, if using a specific version tag:

docker build -t hitstor:1.1.0 \
  --build-arg VERSION=1.1.0 \
  --build-arg COMMIT=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) \
  --build-arg DATE=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d) .

Update the HITSTOR_VERSION variable in your .env file, then:

docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml down
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d

Verify:

docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml exec hitstor hitstor version

Repository data in the /var/lib/hitstor volume is preserved across container restarts.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
Run the new installer over the existing installation. The NSIS installer overwrites the previous binary and updates the registry entries while preserving your configuration files in %ProgramData%\HitStor\.

  1. Download the new installer from GitHub Releases.

  2. Run the installer:

    hitstor-x.y.z-windows-amd64-setup.exe

  3. Follow the installation wizard. Use the same installation directory as the previous version.

  4. Open a new PowerShell window and verify:

    hitstor version

For the agent, download and run the agent installer:

hitstor-agent-x.y.z-windows-amd64-setup.exe

If the agent is running as a Windows Service, it is automatically stopped during the upgrade and restarted afterward.

docs.title: Build from Source
docs.text:
Pull the latest changes and rebuild:

cd /path/to/hitstor
git pull
make build
make agent

Replace the installed binaries:

sudo cp bin/hitstor /usr/local/bin/
sudo cp bin/hitstor-agent /usr/local/bin/

Verify:

hitstor version

If running as a systemd service, restart it:

sudo systemctl restart hitstor-server

docs.title: Repository Compatibility
docs.text:
HitStor repositories are forward-compatible. A repository created with an older version can be read and written by any newer version without migration. There is no separate migration command or repository upgrade step.

If a future release ever requires a repository format change, it will be documented in the release notes with explicit migration instructions.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
Linux Quick Install (.run): The .run installer automatically rolls back if post-upgrade verification fails. The previous binary is restored and the service is restarted with the old version — no manual intervention needed.

Other methods: If you need to revert to a previous version, install the older package or binary using the same installation method and restart the service.

Repositories are forward-compatible, so rolling back to an older version is safe as long as no forward-incompatible repository format changes were introduced (which would be documented in the release notes).

docs.title: Windows Agent Installation
docs.text: The HitStor agent is a lightweight binary that sends encrypted, deduplicated backups from a Windows machine to a remote HitStor server over gRPC. The NSIS installer provides an optional checkbox to register the agent as a Windows Service for unattended backups.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Windows 10 (1809+) or Windows Server 2016+
  • Architecture: amd64 or arm64
  • Network access to the HitStor server (default port 8420)
  • Administrator privileges (required for installation and service management)

docs.title: Download
docs.text:
Download the agent installer from the GitHub Releases page:

  • hitstor-agent-x.y.z-windows-amd64-setup.exe

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Run the installer:

    hitstor-agent-x.y.z-windows-amd64-setup.exe

  2. Accept the license agreement.

  3. Choose the installation directory (default: C:\Program Files\HitStor Agent\).
  4. On the Components page, select the components to install:
    • HitStor Agent (required) -- installs the agent binary and configuration.
    • Install as Windows Service (optional) -- registers and starts the agent as a Windows Service for unattended scheduled backups.
  5. Click Install.

The installer performs the following steps:

  • Copies hitstor-agent.exe to the installation directory.
  • Adds the installation directory to the system PATH.
  • Creates a configuration directory at %ProgramData%\HitStor\.
  • Copies agent-config.yaml.example to the configuration directory.
  • Creates a Start Menu shortcut for the uninstaller.
  • If the service component is selected, registers and starts the HitStorAgent Windows Service.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The agent reads configuration from one of these locations:

Location Scope %AppData%\hitstor\config.yaml Per-user configuration %ProgramData%\HitStor\agent-config.yaml System-wide configuration

Copy the example configuration and edit it:

copy "%ProgramData%\HitStor\agent-config.yaml.example" "%ProgramData%\HitStor\agent-config.yaml"
notepad "%ProgramData%\HitStor\agent-config.yaml"

docs.title: Required Settings
docs.text:
At minimum, configure the server address and API key:

agent_server: "backup-server.internal:8420"
agent_api_key: "your-64-char-hex-api-key"

docs.title: Full Example
docs.text:
agent_server: "backup-server.internal:8420"
agent_api_key: "your-64-char-hex-api-key"
agent_ca_cert: "C:\\certs\\ca.crt"
agent_hostname: "win-workstation-01"
agent_paths:
  - "C:\\Users"
  - "C:\\Data"
agent_excludes:
  - "*.tmp"
  - "Thumbs.db"
  - "desktop.ini"

docs.title: Verify the Installation
docs.text:
Open a new PowerShell window and run:

hitstor-agent version

Test connectivity to the server:

hitstor-agent ping --server backup-server.internal:8420 --ca-cert C:\certs\ca.crt

docs.title: Running a Manual Backup
docs.text:
hitstor-agent backup C:\Users C:\Data

Or with explicit flags:

hitstor-agent backup --server backup-server:8420 --api-key <key> --ca-cert ca.crt C:\Users C:\Data

docs.title: Windows Service Management
docs.text: The agent can run as a Windows Service for unattended scheduled backups. Administrator privileges are required for all service operations.

docs.title: Install the Service
docs.text:
If you did not select the service component during installation, you can install it manually:

hitstor-agent service install --server backup-server:8420 --api-key <key>

Options:

Flag Default Description --name HitStorAgent Windows Service name --display HitStor Backup Agent Display name in the Services console --config (auto-detected) Path to the configuration file

docs.title: Start and Stop
docs.text:
hitstor-agent service start
hitstor-agent service stop

You can also manage the service through the Windows Services console (services.msc).

docs.title: Uninstall the Service
docs.text:
hitstor-agent service stop
hitstor-agent service uninstall

docs.title: Service Behavior
docs.text: When running as a service, the agent reads all settings from the configuration file (agent_server, agent_api_key, agent_paths, etc.) and performs a single backup pass. To schedule recurring backups, configure the service start type or use Windows Task Scheduler.

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text: Area Limitation UID / GID Always stored as 0. Windows has no Unix ownership model. File mode Simplified: 0666 for normal files, 0444 for read-only. Not Unix permissions. CTime Represents file creation time on Windows (not change time as on Unix). Symlinks Require Developer Mode or admin privileges. Skipped if unavailable. NTFS Alternate Data Streams Not backed up. Windows ACLs Not backed up. Permissions are not preserved during restore. Long paths (>260 chars) Supported via Go 1.24 long path handling.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
Use Add/Remove Programs in Windows Settings, or run the uninstaller directly:

& "$env:ProgramFiles\HitStor Agent\uninstall.exe"

The uninstaller stops and removes the Windows Service (if installed), removes the binary, PATH entry, Start Menu shortcuts, and registry entries.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Getting Started -- learn the full backup lifecycle.
  • Configuration -- config file schema and environment variables.

docs.title: Windows Server Installation
docs.text: HitStor provides an NSIS installer for deploying the backup server on Windows. The installer adds hitstor.exe to the system PATH, creates the configuration directory, registers HitStor as a Windows Service, and registers an uninstaller in Add/Remove Programs.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Windows 10 (1809+) or Windows Server 2016+
  • Architecture: amd64
  • Administrator privileges (required for installation)

docs.title: Download
docs.text:
Download the server installer from the GitHub Releases page:

  • hitstor-x.y.z-windows-amd64-setup.exe

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Run the installer:

    hitstor-x.y.z-windows-amd64-setup.exe

  2. Accept the license agreement.

  3. Choose the installation directory (default: C:\Program Files\HitStor\).
  4. Choose the components (both selected by default):
    • Windows Firewall rules -- allow inbound TCP 8420 (agents) and 8421 (dashboard) for hitstor.exe.
    • Install as Windows Service -- register and start the HitStor service.
  5. Click Install.

The installer performs the following steps:

  • Stops the HitStor service if it is already installed (upgrade).
  • Copies hitstor.exe to the installation directory and adds it to the system PATH.
  • Creates %ProgramData%\HitStor\, restricted to Administrators and SYSTEM, with config.yaml.example.
  • Creates %ProgramData%\HitStor\config.yaml from the example if it does not exist (an existing one is preserved).
  • Registers the HitStor Windows Service, which runs hitstor serve --config %ProgramData%\HitStor\config.yaml as LocalSystem with automatic start, and starts it.
  • Registers the application in Add/Remove Programs.

docs.title: Unattended install and upgrade
docs.text:
Run the installer with /S from an elevated prompt. All components are installed, and running the same command with a newer installer upgrades in place (the service is stopped, the binary replaced, and the service re-registered and started):

.\hitstor-x.y.z-windows-amd64-setup.exe /S

docs.title: Verify the Installation
docs.text:
Open a new PowerShell or Command Prompt window (required so the updated PATH takes effect) and run:

hitstor version
Get-Service HitStor

hitstor version prints the version, commit hash, and build date.

docs.title: First Login
docs.text:
With no repositories configured, the server starts in setup mode (dashboard only) and serves it over plain HTTP. Open http://<server>:8421. HTTPS (self-signed by default) is enabled once a repository is configured and the service restarts.

There is no default dashboard password. If config.yaml has none, the server generates one on first start, saves its hash to config.yaml, and logs the plaintext once to %ProgramData%\HitStor\logs\server.log. Read it on the server from an elevated PowerShell:

Select-String -Path "$env:ProgramData\HitStor\logs\server.log" -Pattern "generated one" |
  Select-Object -Last 1 |
  ForEach-Object { ($_.Line | ConvertFrom-Json).fields.password }

Log in with it and change it under Settings. Then create a repository from the Storage page. To reset a lost password, see Dashboard Password.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Edit %ProgramData%\HitStor\config.yaml (see config.yaml.example in the same folder for all options) and restart the service:

notepad "$env:ProgramData\HitStor\config.yaml"
Restart-Service HitStor

docs.title: Managing the Service
docs.text:
The installer manages the service for you. To do it by hand (elevated prompt):

hitstor service install --config "$env:ProgramData\HitStor\config.yaml"
hitstor service start
hitstor service stop
hitstor service uninstall

All subcommands accept --name (default HitStor). You can also use Start-Service/Stop-Service HitStor or the Services console. The service writes to %ProgramData%\HitStor\logs\server.log.

To run the server in the foreground instead (for troubleshooting), stop the service and run:

hitstor serve --config "$env:ProgramData\HitStor\config.yaml"

docs.title: Firewall Configuration
docs.text:
The Windows Firewall rules component creates the rules HitStor Server gRPC (8420) and HitStor Server Dashboard (8421), open to any remote address. To restrict them, for example to an admin network:

Set-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "HitStor Server Dashboard" -RemoteAddress 10.0.0.0/24

If you skipped that component, create the rules yourself:

New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "HitStor gRPC" -Direction Inbound -LocalPort 8420 -Protocol TCP -Action Allow
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "HitStor Dashboard" -Direction Inbound -LocalPort 8421 -Protocol TCP -Action Allow

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
Use Add/Remove Programs in Windows Settings, or run the uninstaller directly:

& "$env:ProgramFiles\HitStor\uninstall.exe"

The uninstaller stops and removes the service and firewall rules, and removes the binary, PATH entry, Start Menu shortcuts, and registry entries. Configuration files in %ProgramData%\HitStor\ and repository data are not deleted.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Windows Agent Installation -- install the agent on Windows workstations.
  • Getting Started -- create your first backup.
  • Configuration -- config file options and environment variables.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text: Technical reference documentation for HitStor.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text: Section Description Server Commands Complete reference for all hitstor CLI commands Agent Commands Complete reference for all hitstor-agent CLI commands Internals Encryption, chunking, deduplication, and repository format Config Reference All configuration keys with types, defaults, and descriptions Environment Variables Environment variables recognized by HitStor gRPC API BackupService and AgentService protocols Dashboard HTTP API Embedded dashboard JSON and SSE endpoints Plugin Development Guide for developing storage, notifier, hook, and scanner plugins

docs.title: gRPC API Reference
docs.text:
Moved

This page has been renamed to gRPC API Reference. Dashboard HTTP endpoints are documented in Dashboard HTTP API.

HitStor uses gRPC over TLS for communication between components. There are two gRPC services:

  • BackupService — server-side, handles agent-to-server backup operations (internal/proto/hitstor/v1/backup.proto)
  • AgentService — agent-side, handles server-to-agent management operations (internal/proto/hitstor/v1/agent.proto)

docs.title: Service: BackupService
docs.text: RPC Type Description BeginSession Unary Start a backup session, receive chunker parameters and IDKey CheckBlobs Unary Check which blob IDs the server already has (batch) UploadChunks Client streaming Stream compressed chunks to the server FinalizeBackup Unary Send file tree, create snapshot, end session Ping Unary Health check, returns server version GetSchedule Unary Query backup schedule for this agent

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
All BackupService RPCs (except Ping) require a valid API key. The key is a 64-character hex string, either generated by hitstor serve agent add <name> (CLI) or sent to the agent during dashboard registration.

  • BeginSession and GetSchedule: API key is sent in the request message (api_key field)
  • CheckBlobs, UploadChunks, FinalizeBackup: Authenticated by session_id from BeginSession
  • Ping: No authentication required

docs.title: Backup Flow
docs.text:
Agent                                          Server
  |                                              |
  |-- BeginSession(api_key, hostname, paths) --> |
  |<-- session_id, id_key, chunker params -------|
  |                                              |
  |  [scan files, chunk with FastCDC,            |
  |   compute blob IDs with id_key]              |
  |                                              |
  |-- CheckBlobs(session_id, blob_ids[]) ------> |
  |<-- needed_ids[] -----------------------------|
  |  (repeat in batches of ~1000)                |
  |                                              |
  |-- UploadChunks(stream) --------------------> |
  |   [blob_id + compressed_data per chunk]      |
  |<-- chunks_received, bytes_received ----------|
  |                                              |
  |-- FinalizeBackup(session_id, files[]) ------> |
  |<-- snapshot_id, stats -----------------------|

docs.title: BeginSession
docs.text:
Starts a backup session for an authenticated agent.

Request: BeginSessionRequest

Field Type Description api_key string 64-character hex API key hostname string Hostname of the machine being backed up paths repeated string Absolute paths being backed up excludes repeated string Glob patterns to exclude tags repeated string Optional snapshot tags

Response: BeginSessionResponse

Field Type Description session_id string Unique session identifier id_key bytes 32-byte HMAC-SHA256 key for computing blob IDs chunker_min uint32 Minimum chunk size in bytes (default: 262144) chunker_avg uint32 Average chunk size in bytes (default: 1048576) chunker_max uint32 Maximum chunk size in bytes (default: 4194304)

docs.title: CheckBlobs
docs.text:
Checks which blob IDs the server already has. Called in batches (recommended: 1000 IDs per call).

Request: CheckBlobsRequest

Field Type Description session_id string Session from BeginSession blob_ids repeated bytes Batch of 32-byte blob IDs to check

Response: CheckBlobsResponse

Field Type Description needed_ids repeated bytes Blob IDs the server does NOT have (upload these)

docs.title: UploadChunks
docs.text:
Streams compressed chunks to the server. Client-side streaming RPC -- the agent sends multiple UploadChunkMessage messages on a single stream.

Request (stream): UploadChunkMessage

Field Type Description session_id string Session from BeginSession blob_id bytes 32-byte blob ID (HMAC-SHA256 of uncompressed data) compressed_data bytes Zstd-compressed chunk data uncompressed_length uint32 Original uncompressed size in bytes

Response: UploadChunksResponse

Field Type Description chunks_received uint32 Total chunks received and stored bytes_received uint64 Total compressed bytes received

docs.title: FinalizeBackup
docs.text:
Sends the complete file/directory tree and closes the session. The server builds tree blobs, creates a snapshot, and returns summary statistics.

Request: FinalizeBackupRequest

Field Type Description session_id string Session from BeginSession files repeated FileNode Complete directory tree

FileNode fields:

Field Type Description path string Relative path (forward slashes, no leading slash) is_dir bool true for directories mode uint32 Unix file mode (permissions) mtime_ns int64 Modification time (nanoseconds since Unix epoch) size int64 File size in bytes (0 for directories) uid uint32 Owner user ID gid uint32 Owner group ID content_ids repeated bytes Ordered chunk blob IDs (files only) link_target string Symlink target path (symlinks only)

Response: FinalizeBackupResponse

Field Type Description snapshot_id string 8-character hex prefix of the snapshot ID files_new uint64 Number of new files files_unchanged uint64 Number of unchanged files bytes_added uint64 New data added to repository bytes_processed uint64 Total data processed duration_seconds double Backup duration

docs.title: Ping
docs.text:
Health check RPC. No authentication required.

Request: PingRequest (empty)

Response: PingResponse

Field Type Description version string HitStor server version repo_id string 64-character hex repository ID

docs.title: GetSchedule
docs.text:
Returns the backup schedule configured for this agent.

Request: GetScheduleRequest

Field Type Description api_key string 64-character hex API key

Response: GetScheduleResponse

Field Type Description enabled bool Whether scheduled backups are enabled interval_hours int32 Interval between backups in hours next_run_unix int64 Next backup time (Unix seconds, 0 if disabled)

docs.title: Transport
docs.text:
• Protocol: gRPC over TLS (required)
  • Port: 8420 (default, configurable via serve_port)
  • TLS: Server generates self-signed certificate if none provided; agents can use --ca-cert to trust custom CAs
  • Max message size: ~2 GiB (set by go-plugin framework; pack files cap at 128 MiB)

docs.title: Error Codes
docs.text: gRPC Code Meaning Unauthenticated Invalid or missing API key NotFound Unknown session ID FailedPrecondition Pre-backup hook rejected the operation Internal Server-side error (check logs)

docs.title: Service: AgentService
docs.text:
The AgentService runs on each agent (default port 8422) and handles server-to-agent management operations. The server connects to this service when adding agents from the dashboard, browsing filesystems, or configuring backup paths.

RPC Type Description Register Unary Register the agent with a server (send API key + server address) ListDirectory Unary List files and directories at a path on the agent Configure Unary Set backup paths and exclude patterns on the agent AgentInfo Unary Query agent hostname, version, OS, paths, and registration status

docs.title: AgentService Authentication
docs.text: All AgentService RPCs require a valid agent token — a 64-character hex string generated during agent installation. The token is sent in the token field of each request message.

docs.title: Register
docs.text:
Called by the server when an admin adds the agent from the dashboard. The server sends an API key and its address; the agent stores them and starts the backup loop.

Request: RegisterRequest

Field Type Description token string 64-character hex agent token api_key string API key for agent-to-server backup authentication server_addr string Server address (host:port) for backup push server_ca_cert bytes PEM-encoded TLS certificate (optional)

Response: RegisterResponse

Field Type Description hostname string Agent machine hostname version string Agent binary version os string Operating system (for example, linux) arch string Architecture (for example, amd64)

docs.title: ListDirectory
docs.text:
Browse the agent's filesystem. Called when the admin expands a directory in the dashboard's filesystem tree browser.

Request: ListDirectoryRequest

Field Type Description token string 64-character hex agent token path string Absolute path to list (empty string returns root-level directories)

Response: ListDirectoryResponse

Field Type Description entries repeated DirEntry Directory entries, sorted directories-first

DirEntry fields:

Field Type Description name string Entry name path string Absolute path is_dir bool true for directories size int64 File size in bytes (0 for directories) mode uint32 Unix file mode readable bool Whether the agent process can read this path has_children bool Whether this directory contains subdirectories (hint for UI expand icon)

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
Set backup paths and exclude patterns on the agent. Called when the admin clicks "Save Backup Paths" in the dashboard.

Request: ConfigureRequest

Field Type Description token string 64-character hex agent token backup_paths repeated string Absolute paths to back up excludes repeated string Glob patterns to exclude

Response: ConfigureResponse

Field Type Description success bool Whether the configuration was saved message string Status message

docs.title: AgentInfo
docs.text:
Query the agent's current state.

Request: AgentInfoRequest

Field Type Description token string 64-character hex agent token

Response: AgentInfoResponse

Field Type Description hostname string Agent machine hostname version string Agent binary version os string Operating system arch string Architecture backup_paths repeated string Currently configured backup paths excludes repeated string Currently configured exclude patterns registered bool Whether the agent is registered with a server server_addr string Registered server address (empty if not registered)

docs.title: AgentService Transport
docs.text:
• Protocol: gRPC over TLS (self-signed, auto-generated by the agent)
  • Port: 8422 (default, configurable via --listen-port or HITSTOR_AGENT_LISTEN_PORT)
  • TLS: Agent generates a self-signed certificate; the server uses InsecureSkipVerify since the token provides authentication

docs.text:

  • Plugin Development — plugin gRPC protocols

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text: Complete reference for all HitStor configuration keys. Configuration is stored in YAML format at ~/.config/hitstor/config.yaml (Linux) or %AppData%\hitstor\config.yaml (Windows).

docs.title: Precedence
docs.text:
Values are resolved in this order (highest priority first):

  1. CLI flag -- --repo /path
  2. Environment variable -- HITSTOR_REPO=/path
  3. Config file -- repo: /path
  4. Default value

docs.title: Core Settings
docs.text: Key Type Default CLI Flag Env Var Description repo string --repo HITSTOR_REPO Repository location (local path, s3:endpoint/bucket, or plugin:name/args) password_file string --password-file Path to file containing the repository password parallel int 0 --parallel Number of parallel workers (0 = auto-detect based on CPU count) exclude list Global exclude patterns (applied to all backups)

docs.title: S3 Backend
docs.text: Key Type Default CLI Flag Description s3_access_key string --s3-access-key S3 access key (sensitive -- masked in config show) s3_secret_key string --s3-secret-key S3 secret key (sensitive -- masked in config show) s3_region string us-east-1 --s3-region S3 region

docs.title: Server Settings
docs.text:
Used by hitstor serve to configure the gRPC server and web dashboard.

Key Type Default CLI Flag Description serve_port int 8420 --port gRPC server listen port serve_tls_cert string --tls-cert Path to TLS certificate file serve_tls_key string --tls-key Path to TLS private key file serve_dashboard_port int 8421 --dashboard-port HTTP dashboard listen port serve_dashboard_password string Dashboard login password (sensitive -- if empty, a random one is generated at startup and logged once; see Dashboard Password) serve_dashboard_language string Default dashboard language code (en, es). Empty uses the browser language; users can still switch with the selector. See Translations serve_advertise_addr string --advertise-addr Address advertised to agents for registration (use when server is behind NAT) update_check bool true Enable automatic version checks. When enabled, the server checks for updates every 24 hours and shows a banner in the dashboard. update_url string Custom update check URL (empty = GitHub Releases API)

docs.title: Alerting
docs.text: Key Type Default Description alert_webhook_url string Webhook URL for alert notifications (receives POST with JSON payload) alert_stale_threshold int 25 Hours before an agent is considered stale (minimum: 1) alert_notifier_plugins list Notifier plugin names to load for alert delivery

docs.title: Agent Settings
docs.text:
Used by hitstor-agent to configure the remote backup agent.

Key Type Default CLI Flag Env Var Description agent_server string --server HITSTOR_AGENT_SERVER Remote server address (host:port) agent_api_key string --api-key HITSTOR_AGENT_API_KEY Agent API key for authentication (sensitive -- 64-char hex) agent_ca_cert string --ca-cert Path to CA certificate for TLS verification agent_hostname string --hostname Override hostname sent to server (defaults to system hostname) agent_paths list Default backup paths (used when no paths given on command line) agent_excludes list Default exclude patterns for agent backups

docs.title: Plugin Settings
docs.text: Key Type Default Description plugin_dir string Directory to search for plugin binaries (searched before $PATH) hook_plugins list Hook plugin names to load for pre/post-backup lifecycle events fs_scanner_plugin string Filesystem scanner plugin name (builtin or a custom Scanner plugin; only one active at a time)

docs.title: Integrations (integrations)
docs.text:
Used by Sentinel (Gemini). Sensitive values are stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM, base64) using the repository encryption key. Editable from the dashboard Settings → Integrations tab.

Key Type Description gemini_api_key_encrypted string Encrypted Gemini API key for Sentinel (and GEMINI_API_KEY env export) gemini_model string Gemini model (default: gemini-1.5-pro)

GEMINI_API_KEY still works and takes precedence when set. Use Import from environment in Settings to migrate it to encrypted YAML.

docs.title: Ignored legacy keys
docs.text: Microsoft 365 (m365_*), cloud provider (gcp_project, aws_role_arn, aws_region, azure_tenant, azure_client, azure_sub), and collector_plugins keys were removed from the config schema in v2.0.0. Existing config.yaml files containing them still load — YAML silently ignores unknown keys — but the values are never read. Remove these keys at your convenience.

docs.title: Sentinel (sentinel)
docs.text: Optional Sentinel telemetry settings (future dashboard editing). Keys mirror HITSTOR_SENTINEL_* environment variables.

docs.title: Multi-Repository (repositories)
docs.text:
When running hitstor serve with multiple repositories, define a list instead of a single repo:

repositories:
  - name: production
    type: local
    path: /var/lib/hitstor/prod-repo
    password_file: /etc/hitstor/prod-password

  - name: offsite
    type: s3
    endpoint: s3.amazonaws.com
    bucket: company-backups
    region: us-east-1
    access_key_encrypted: <base64 AES-256-GCM ciphertext>
    secret_key_encrypted: <base64 AES-256-GCM ciphertext>
    password_file: /etc/hitstor/s3-repo-password

S3 credentials are stored encrypted in the config file. The dashboard Storage page can create repositories without hand-editing ciphertext.

If repositories is empty and repo is set, the server runs in single-repository legacy mode.

docs.title: Key Types
docs.text: Type Description Management Commands string Single value config set, config unset int Integer value config set, config unset list Ordered list of values config add, config remove

docs.title: Local Server
docs.text:
repo: /var/lib/hitstor/repo
parallel: 4
exclude:
  - "*.tmp"
  - ".cache"
serve_port: 8420
serve_tls_cert: /etc/hitstor/tls/cert.pem
serve_tls_key: /etc/hitstor/tls/key.pem
serve_dashboard_port: 8421
serve_dashboard_password: changeme
alert_webhook_url: https://hooks.slack.com/services/T.../B.../xxx
alert_stale_threshold: 25

docs.title: Remote Agent
docs.text:
agent_server: backup.internal:8420
agent_api_key: a1b2c3d4e5f6...  # 64-char hex
agent_ca_cert: /etc/hitstor/ca.pem
agent_paths:
  - /etc
  - /home
  - /var/lib
agent_excludes:
  - "*.log"
  - "/home/*/.cache"

docs.title: S3 Backend
docs.text:
repo: s3:s3.amazonaws.com/my-backup-bucket
s3_access_key: AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
s3_secret_key: wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY
s3_region: us-west-2

docs.text:

  • Environment Variables -- all environment variables

docs.title: Dashboard HTTP API
docs.text:
The embedded dashboard served by hitstor serve exposes a JSON API on the HTTP port (default 8421). Routes are defined in internal/dashboard/dashboard.go.

Unless noted, endpoints require dashboard authentication when serve_dashboard_password is set. Session cookies are issued via POST /login.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text:
Path Description GET / Overview GET /backups Backup jobs list GET /backups/{id} Backup job detail GET /agents Agents GET /agents/{name} Agent detail GET /snapshots/{id} Snapshot detail (browse + restore) GET /storage Repository management GET /storage/{name} Repository detail GET /restores Restore sessions GET /settings Server settings (General, Security/TLS, Network, Integrations, Notifications)

GET /snapshots redirects to /storage.

docs.title: Agents
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /api/agents List agents with status and schedule info POST /api/agents Register agent (manual entry: name, agent_addr, optional api_key) DELETE /api/agents/{name} Remove agent POST /api/agents/{name}/schedule Set schedule (interval, cron, timezone, jobs) POST /api/agents/{name}/repo Set target repository POST /api/agents/{name}/browse Browse agent filesystem POST /api/agents/{name}/configure Set backup paths and excludes GET /api/agents/{name}/info Agent info POST /api/agents/{name}/suspend Suspend agent backups POST /api/agents/{name}/unsuspend Unsuspend agent

docs.title: Agent Discovery
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /api/discover/subnets List local subnets for scanning POST /api/discover/scan Scan subnet for agents POST /api/discover/probe Probe a specific host:port

docs.title: Backup Jobs
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /api/backups List backup jobs POST /api/backups Create job (job_type is always files) GET /api/backups/{id} Get job PUT /api/backups/{id} Update job DELETE /api/backups/{id} Delete job POST /api/backups/{id}/run Run job now POST /api/backups/{id}/cancel Cancel running backup GET /api/backups/validate-cron Validate cron expression GET /api/timezones List supported timezones

docs.title: Repositories & Storage
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /api/repos List repositories POST /api/repos Create repository (local or S3) DELETE /api/repos/{name} Disconnect repository GET /api/disk-space?path= Disk space for a path POST /api/repos/test-s3 Test S3 credentials POST /api/repos/detect Detect existing repo at path GET /api/repos/{name}/growth Growth chart data (?range=, ?granularity=) POST /api/repos/{name}/check Start integrity check POST /api/repos/{name}/prune Start prune GET /api/repos/{name}/sessions Active sessions for repo

docs.title: Snapshots & Restore
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /api/snapshots?host=&limit= List snapshots (newest first) GET /api/snapshots/{id}/tree?path= Browse snapshot file tree POST /api/snapshots/{id}/restore Start agent restore (agent_name, target_path, optional includes) GET /api/restores List restore sessions GET /api/restore/{id}/events SSE restore progress

docs.title: Progress & Operations
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /api/stats Repository statistics GET /api/active-backups Active backup sessions GET /api/backup-progress/events SSE backup progress (all sessions) GET /api/operations/{id}/events SSE for check/prune operations

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /api/settings Effective server settings (secrets masked) PUT /api/settings/general update_check, update_url, parallel, sync_writes, min_free_reserve_bytes PUT /api/settings/security dashboard_password (empty = keep current); may set restart_required PUT /api/settings/network serve_port, serve_dashboard_port, serve_advertise_addr; may set restart_required PUT /api/settings/notifications alert_webhook_url, alert_stale_threshold, alert_notifier_plugins PUT /api/settings/integrations Gemini key/model (gemini_api_key empty = keep current) POST /api/settings/integrations/import-env Migrate GEMINI_API_KEY into encrypted YAML GET /api/settings/tls/status TLS certificate metadata (source, expiry, SANs) POST /api/settings/tls/upload Multipart cert + key PEM files; sets restart_required POST /api/settings/test/gemini Validate Gemini API key POST /api/settings/test/webhook POST test payload to configured webhook URL

docs.title: Alerts (Sentinel)
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /api/alerts List sentinel/security alerts POST /api/alerts/{id}/resolve Resolve alert

docs.title: Metrics (unauthenticated)
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /metrics Prometheus text exposition

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /login Login page POST /login Submit password POST /logout End session

  • Dashboard — UI overview

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: HitStor reads the following environment variables. Environment variables override config file values but are overridden by CLI flags.

docs.title: Server (hitstor)
docs.text: Variable Config Key Description HITSTOR_REPO repo Repository location (local path, s3:endpoint/bucket, or plugin:name/args) HITSTOR_PASSWORD -- Repository password (no config key -- only env var or interactive prompt) HITSTOR_PASSWORD_FILE password_file Path to file containing the repository password

docs.title: Agent (hitstor-agent)
docs.text: Variable Config Key Description HITSTOR_AGENT_LISTEN_PORT agent_listen_port gRPC listen port for dashboard management (default: 8422) HITSTOR_AGENT_SERVER agent_server Remote server address (host:port) — set automatically for dashboard-managed agents HITSTOR_AGENT_API_KEY agent_api_key Agent API key for authentication — set automatically for dashboard-managed agents

docs.title: Server with environment variables
docs.text:
export HITSTOR_REPO=/var/lib/hitstor/repo
export HITSTOR_PASSWORD=mysecretpassword
hitstor serve --port 8420 --tls-cert cert.pem --tls-key key.pem

docs.title: Agent with environment variables
docs.text:
export HITSTOR_AGENT_SERVER=backup.internal:8420
export HITSTOR_AGENT_API_KEY=a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2
hitstor-agent backup /etc /home

docs.title: Systemd environment file
docs.text:
Both the server and agent systemd units support environment files:

# /etc/hitstor/server.env
HITSTOR_REPO=/var/lib/hitstor/repo
HITSTOR_PASSWORD=mysecretpassword

# /etc/hitstor/agent.env (dashboard-managed)
HITSTOR_AGENT_LISTEN_PORT=8422

# /etc/hitstor/agent.env (legacy)
# HITSTOR_AGENT_SERVER=backup.internal:8420
# HITSTOR_AGENT_API_KEY=a1b2c3d4...

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
docker run -e HITSTOR_REPO=/data/repo \
           -e HITSTOR_PASSWORD=mysecretpassword \
           hitstor:latest serve

docs.title: Integrations (server)
docs.text:
These variables override the corresponding integrations.* keys in config.yaml when set. Prefer encrypted YAML in production; use Settings → Import from environment to migrate values into the config file.

Variable Config Key Description GEMINI_API_KEY integrations.gemini_api_key_encrypted Gemini API key for Sentinel (plaintext env; stored encrypted when imported)

When both env vars and YAML are set, environment variables take precedence. After import, secrets in YAML are encrypted and the env vars can be removed.

docs.title: Ignored legacy variables
docs.text:
HITSTOR_M365_*, HITSTOR_GCP_PROJECT, HITSTOR_AWS_ROLE_ARN, HITSTOR_AWS_REGION, and HITSTOR_AZURE_SUB are no longer read since v2.0.0, when SaaS, database, and cloud-VM backup were removed from the product. Setting them has no effect.

HITSTOR_AZURE_TENANT and HITSTOR_AZURE_CLIENT are still read, but their meaning changed: they no longer configure cloud-VM discovery — they now authenticate Sentinel's optional Azure Blob retention lock (see below).

docs.title: Sentinel (server)
docs.text:
Sentinel is configured entirely through environment variables, read once at hitstor serve startup — there is no hitstor config set equivalent. The Gemini API key/model fall back to the integrations.* values above when unset here.

Variable Default Description HITSTOR_SENTINEL_ENABLED true Set to false to disable Sentinel entirely HITSTOR_SENTINEL_MODEL integrations.gemini_model, else gemini-1.5-flash Gemini model used for threat analysis HITSTOR_SENTINEL_API_KEY integrations.gemini_api_key_encrypted Gemini API key for Sentinel (falls back to the shared Gemini key) HITSTOR_SENTINEL_THRESHOLD 0.8 Confidence (0-1) above which a detected threat triggers containment HITSTOR_SENTINEL_RETENTION_DAYS 30 Retention period applied when Sentinel locks a storage bucket HITSTOR_SENTINEL_BACKEND_TYPE gcs Which storage backend's retention lock to use: gcs, s3, or azure HITSTOR_GCS_BUCKET GCS bucket to lock (when BACKEND_TYPE=gcs) HITSTOR_S3_BUCKET S3 bucket to lock (when BACKEND_TYPE=s3) HITSTOR_S3_REGION S3 bucket region HITSTOR_S3_ROLE_ARN AWS role to assume for the S3 Object Lock API call HITSTOR_AZURE_CONTAINER Azure Blob container to lock (when BACKEND_TYPE=azure) HITSTOR_AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT Azure storage account name HITSTOR_AZURE_TENANT Azure AD tenant ID for the retention-lock API call HITSTOR_AZURE_CLIENT Azure AD client ID for the retention-lock API call

The retention lock only fires when Sentinel detects a threat above the confidence threshold — it does not run on every backup. See Ransomware Sentinel.

docs.title: Notes
