docs.text:
• The repository password can be provided via --password, --password-file, HITSTOR_PASSWORD, HITSTOR_PASSWORD_FILE, or the config file password_file key. CLI flags take highest precedence.
  • HITSTOR_PASSWORD_FILE takes precedence over HITSTOR_PASSWORD if both are set.
  • Sensitive values (s3_access_key, s3_secret_key, agent_api_key, serve_dashboard_password) do not have dedicated environment variables -- use the config file or CLI flags.

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• Configuration Reference -- all config keys
  • Configuration Guide -- usage tutorial

docs.title: gRPC API Reference
docs.text:
Note

For the embedded dashboard JSON API, see Dashboard HTTP API.

HitStor uses gRPC over TLS for communication between components. There are two gRPC services:

  • BackupService — server-side, handles agent-to-server backup operations (internal/proto/hitstor/v1/backup.proto)
  • AgentService — agent-side, handles server-to-agent management operations (internal/proto/hitstor/v1/agent.proto)

docs.title: Service: BackupService
docs.text: RPC Type Description BeginSession Unary Start a backup session, receive chunker parameters and IDKey CheckBlobs Unary Check which blob IDs the server already has (batch) UploadChunks Client streaming Stream compressed chunks to the server FinalizeBackup Unary Send file tree, create snapshot, end session Ping Unary Health check, returns server version GetSchedule Unary Query backup schedule for this agent

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
All BackupService RPCs (except Ping) require a valid API key. The key is a 64-character hex string, either generated by hitstor serve agent add <name> (CLI) or sent to the agent during dashboard registration.

  • BeginSession and GetSchedule: API key is sent in the request message (api_key field)
  • CheckBlobs, UploadChunks, FinalizeBackup: Authenticated by session_id from BeginSession
  • Ping: No authentication required

docs.title: Backup Flow
docs.text:
Agent                                          Server
  |                                              |
  |-- BeginSession(api_key, hostname, paths) --> |
  |<-- session_id, id_key, chunker params -------|
  |                                              |
  |  [scan files, chunk with FastCDC,            |
  |   compute blob IDs with id_key]              |
  |                                              |
  |-- CheckBlobs(session_id, blob_ids[]) ------> |
  |<-- needed_ids[] -----------------------------|
  |  (repeat in batches of ~1000)                |
  |                                              |
  |-- UploadChunks(stream) --------------------> |
  |   [blob_id + compressed_data per chunk]      |
  |<-- chunks_received, bytes_received ----------|
  |                                              |
  |-- FinalizeBackup(session_id, files[]) ------> |
  |<-- snapshot_id, stats -----------------------|

docs.title: BeginSession
docs.text:
Starts a backup session for an authenticated agent.

Request: BeginSessionRequest

Field Type Description api_key string 64-character hex API key hostname string Hostname of the machine being backed up paths repeated string Absolute paths being backed up excludes repeated string Glob patterns to exclude tags repeated string Optional snapshot tags job_id string Backup job ID (links session to a dashboard job)

Response: BeginSessionResponse

Field Type Description session_id string Unique session identifier id_key bytes 32-byte HMAC-SHA256 key for computing blob IDs chunker_min uint32 Minimum chunk size in bytes (default: 262144) chunker_avg uint32 Average chunk size in bytes (default: 1048576) chunker_max uint32 Maximum chunk size in bytes (default: 4194304) previous_files repeated PreviousFileEntry Metadata from parent snapshot for incremental detection parent_snapshot_id string Hex ID of parent snapshot (empty for full backup)

PreviousFileEntry fields: path, mtime_ns, size, content_ids (ordered chunk blob IDs).

docs.title: CheckBlobs
docs.text:
Checks which blob IDs the server already has. Called in batches (recommended: 1000 IDs per call).

Request: CheckBlobsRequest

Field Type Description session_id string Session from BeginSession blob_ids repeated bytes Batch of 32-byte blob IDs to check

Response: CheckBlobsResponse

Field Type Description needed_ids repeated bytes Blob IDs the server does NOT have (upload these)

docs.title: UploadChunks
docs.text:
Streams compressed chunks to the server. Client-side streaming RPC -- the agent sends multiple UploadChunkMessage messages on a single stream.

Request (stream): UploadChunkMessage

Field Type Description session_id string Session from BeginSession blob_id bytes 32-byte blob ID (HMAC-SHA256 of uncompressed data) compressed_data bytes Zstd-compressed chunk data uncompressed_length uint32 Original uncompressed size in bytes

Response: UploadChunksResponse

Field Type Description chunks_received uint32 Total chunks received and stored bytes_received uint64 Total compressed bytes received

docs.title: FinalizeBackup
docs.text:
Sends the complete file/directory tree and closes the session. The server builds tree blobs, creates a snapshot, and returns summary statistics.

Request: FinalizeBackupRequest

Field Type Description session_id string Session from BeginSession files repeated FileNode Complete directory tree backup_type string "full" or "incremental" parent_snapshot_id string Parent snapshot hex ID (incremental only)

FileNode fields:

Field Type Description path string Relative path (forward slashes, no leading slash) is_dir bool true for directories mode uint32 Unix file mode (permissions) mtime_ns int64 Modification time (nanoseconds since Unix epoch) size int64 File size in bytes (0 for directories) uid uint32 Owner user ID gid uint32 Owner group ID content_ids repeated bytes Ordered chunk blob IDs (files only) link_target string Symlink target path (symlinks only)

Response: FinalizeBackupResponse

Field Type Description snapshot_id string 8-character hex prefix of the snapshot ID files_new uint64 Number of new files files_unchanged uint64 Number of unchanged files bytes_added uint64 New data added to repository bytes_processed uint64 Total data processed duration_seconds double Backup duration

docs.title: Ping
docs.text:
Health check RPC. No authentication required.

Request: PingRequest (empty)

Response: PingResponse

Field Type Description version string HitStor server version repo_id string 64-character hex repository ID

docs.title: GetSchedule
docs.text:
Returns the backup schedule configured for this agent.

Request: GetScheduleRequest

Field Type Description api_key string 64-character hex API key

Response: GetScheduleResponse

Field Type Description enabled bool Legacy: first enabled job (backward compatibility) interval_hours int32 Legacy: interval from first job next_run_unix int64 Legacy: next run from first job jobs repeated ScheduledJob All backup jobs for this agent

ScheduledJob fields: job_id, name, paths, excludes, repo_name, enabled, interval_hours, next_run_unix, run_now, full_rescan_days, last_full_backup_unix, cron_expression, timezone, use_vss.

docs.title: Transport
docs.text:
• Protocol: gRPC over TLS (required)
  • Port: 8420 (default, configurable via serve_port)
  • TLS: Server generates self-signed certificate if none provided; agents can use --ca-cert to trust custom CAs
  • Max message size: ~2 GiB (set by go-plugin framework; pack files cap at 128 MiB)

docs.title: Error Codes
docs.text: gRPC Code Meaning Unauthenticated Invalid or missing API key NotFound Unknown session ID FailedPrecondition Pre-backup hook rejected the operation Internal Server-side error (check logs)

docs.title: Service: AgentService
docs.text:
The AgentService runs on each agent (default port 8422) and handles server-to-agent management operations. The server connects to this service when adding agents from the dashboard, browsing filesystems, or configuring backup paths.

RPC Type Description Register Unary Register the agent with a server (send API key + server address) ListDirectory Unary List files and directories at a path on the agent Configure Unary Set backup paths and exclude patterns on the agent AgentInfo Unary Query agent hostname, version, OS, paths, and registration status RestoreData Client streaming Stream restore data to agent WakeUp Unary Signal agent to check schedule immediately (dashboard "Backup Now")

docs.title: AgentService Authentication
docs.text: All AgentService RPCs require a valid agent token — a 64-character hex string generated during agent installation. The token is sent in the token field of each request message.

docs.title: Register
docs.text:
Called by the server when an admin adds the agent from the dashboard. The server sends an API key and its address; the agent stores them and starts the backup loop.

Request: RegisterRequest

Field Type Description token string 64-character hex agent token api_key string API key for agent-to-server backup authentication server_addr string Server address (host:port) for backup push server_ca_cert bytes PEM-encoded TLS certificate (optional)

Response: RegisterResponse

Field Type Description hostname string Agent machine hostname version string Agent binary version os string Operating system (for example, linux) arch string Architecture (for example, amd64)

docs.title: ListDirectory
docs.text:
Browse the agent's filesystem. Called when the admin expands a directory in the dashboard's filesystem tree browser.

Request: ListDirectoryRequest

Field Type Description token string 64-character hex agent token path string Absolute path to list (empty string returns root-level directories)

Response: ListDirectoryResponse

Field Type Description entries repeated DirEntry Directory entries, sorted directories-first

DirEntry fields:

Field Type Description name string Entry name path string Absolute path is_dir bool true for directories size int64 File size in bytes (0 for directories) mode uint32 Unix file mode readable bool Whether the agent process can read this path has_children bool Whether this directory contains subdirectories (hint for UI expand icon)

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
Set backup paths and exclude patterns on the agent. Called when the admin clicks "Save Backup Paths" in the dashboard.

Request: ConfigureRequest

Field Type Description token string 64-character hex agent token backup_paths repeated string Absolute paths to back up excludes repeated string Glob patterns to exclude

Response: ConfigureResponse

Field Type Description success bool Whether the configuration was saved message string Status message

docs.title: AgentInfo
docs.text:
Query the agent's current state.

Request: AgentInfoRequest

Field Type Description token string 64-character hex agent token

Response: AgentInfoResponse

Field Type Description hostname string Agent machine hostname version string Agent binary version os string Operating system arch string Architecture backup_paths repeated string Currently configured backup paths excludes repeated string Currently configured exclude patterns registered bool Whether the agent is registered with a server server_addr string Registered server address (empty if not registered)

docs.title: WakeUp
docs.text:
Called when an admin triggers "Backup Now" from the dashboard so the agent does not wait for the next poll interval.

Request: WakeUpRequest — token (64-char hex agent token)

Response: WakeUpResponse — acknowledged (bool)

docs.title: AgentService Transport
docs.text:
• Protocol: gRPC over TLS (self-signed, auto-generated by the agent)
  • Port: 8422 (default, configurable via --listen-port or HITSTOR_AGENT_LISTEN_PORT)
  • TLS: Agent generates a self-signed certificate; the server uses InsecureSkipVerify since the token provides authentication

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• Internals — encryption, chunking, and deduplication details
  • Plugin Development — plugin gRPC protocols

docs.title: Internals
docs.text: This document describes HitStor's internal design: encryption, chunking, deduplication, pack format, and repository layout.

docs.title: Encryption
docs.text:
All data stored in the repository is encrypted using AES-256-GCM (Galois/Counter Mode), which provides both confidentiality and authentication. The ciphertext format is:

nonce (12 bytes) || ciphertext || authentication tag (16 bytes)

A random 12-byte nonce is generated for each encryption operation.

docs.title: Key Derivation
docs.text:
HitStor uses scrypt to derive a 64-byte key from the user's password:

Parameter Value N (CPU/memory cost) 32768 r (block size) 8 p (parallelism) 1 Salt 64 random bytes Output 64 bytes

The first 32 bytes of the derived key are used as the AES-256-GCM encryption key for the key file. The remaining 32 bytes are not used directly (the master key provides the actual encryption and ID keys).

docs.title: Master Key
docs.text:
Each repository has a master key consisting of two 32-byte keys:

  • EncryptKey -- used for AES-256-GCM encryption of all repository data (packs, indexes, snapshots)
  • IDKey -- used for HMAC-SHA256 blob identification

The master key is generated from 64 cryptographically random bytes and stored in the keys/ directory, encrypted with the password-derived key.

docs.title: Blob IDs
docs.text: Blob IDs are computed as HMAC-SHA256(IDKey, data), producing a 32-byte identifier. This is content-addressable (the same content always produces the same ID) but not guessable without the IDKey, providing privacy even if an attacker can observe blob IDs.

docs.title: Chunking
docs.text:
HitStor uses FastCDC (Fast Content-Defined Chunking) with a Gear rolling hash to split file data into variable-size chunks whose boundaries are determined by the content.

Parameter Value Minimum chunk size 256 KiB Average chunk size 1 MiB Target maximum chunk size 4 MiB

The algorithm uses two-phase boundary detection:

  1. Phase 1 (positions min to avg): uses a more permissive mask (more bits set), making it easier to find a boundary. This biases chunks toward the average size.
  2. Phase 2 (positions avg to max): uses a stricter mask (fewer bits set), allowing chunks to grow past the average when no earlier boundary was found.

If no boundary is found before the maximum size, the chunk is cut at the maximum.

Content-defined chunking means that insertions or deletions in a file only affect nearby chunk boundaries, maximizing deduplication across backups.

docs.title: Deduplication
docs.text:
Deduplication happens at the chunk level. Before writing a new blob to the repository, HitStor checks:

  1. In-session set -- blobs already added during the current backup
  2. Repository index -- the full index of all blobs stored in the repository

For local CLI backups (hitstor backup), an additional layer applies:

  1. Files cache -- SQLite database tracking file inode, size, mtime, and chunk IDs

For remote agent backups, unchanged files are detected via previous snapshot metadata returned in BeginSession (previous_files with mtime, size, content IDs). No agent-side SQLite cache is required.

docs.title: Compression
docs.text: Each chunk is compressed with Zstd (Zstandard) before encryption. Compression is applied per chunk, not per file, which allows individual chunks to be decompressed independently during restore.

docs.title: Pack Files
docs.text:
Blobs are not stored individually. Instead, multiple blobs are grouped into pack files to reduce the number of objects in the backend and improve I/O efficiency.

Parameter Value Pack size threshold 128 MiB

When the accumulated blob data in the current pack exceeds 128 MiB, the pack is finalized and written to the backend. Each pack contains:

  • Concatenated encrypted blob data
  • An encrypted header at the end of the file containing the blob offsets, sizes, types, and IDs

There are two blob types stored in packs:

  • Data blobs -- file content chunks
  • Tree blobs -- directory tree structures

docs.title: Index Files
docs.text:
Index files map blob IDs to their locations within pack files. Each index entry records:

  • The pack ID containing the blob
  • The blob ID, type, offset, and lengths (compressed and uncompressed)

Indexes are written before snapshots for crash consistency: if a crash occurs after writing the index but before writing the snapshot, the orphaned index and pack data will be cleaned up by the next prune.

docs.title: Snapshots
docs.text:
A snapshot records the metadata for a single backup operation:

  • Timestamp
  • Hostname and username
  • Backed-up paths and exclude patterns
  • Tags
  • Root tree blob ID (the entry point for the directory tree)
  • Summary statistics (files new, files unchanged, bytes added, bytes processed, duration)

Snapshots are stored as encrypted JSON files in the snapshots/ directory.

docs.title: Cache
docs.text:
HitStor maintains a local SQLite database for incremental backup performance:

~/.cache/hitstor/<repo-id>/cache.db

The database uses WAL (Write-Ahead Logging) mode and tracks:

  • files -- maps file paths (by SHA-256 hash) to their inode, size, mtime, and chunk IDs. A cache hit (all three metadata fields match) means the file is unchanged and its chunks can be reused without re-reading the file.
  • known_chunks -- records chunk IDs that exist in the repository, avoiding redundant index lookups.
  • meta -- generation counter for cache cleanup.

Each cache open increments a generation counter. Old entries not seen for several generations can be cleaned up.

docs.title: Repository Layout
docs.text:
<repo>/
├── config                          # Unencrypted JSON: repo ID, chunker params
├── data/
│   └── <first-2-hex>/
│       └── <pack-id>              # Encrypted pack files (blobs + header)
├── index/
│   ├── latest                     # Plain-text pointer to consolidated index ID (optional)
│   └── <index-id>                 # Encrypted JSON: blob → pack mapping
├── keys/
│   └── <key-id>                   # Encrypted JSON: master key + KDF params
├── locks/
│   └── <lock-id>                  # Lock files for concurrency control
└── snapshots/
    └── <snapshot-id>              # Encrypted JSON: snapshot metadata + tree ref

All IDs are 32-byte values represented as 64-character hex strings. The data/ directory uses a two-character fan-out prefix (first two hex chars of the pack ID) to avoid excessive directory entries.

docs.title: Repository locking
docs.text:
HitStor uses lock files in locks/ to coordinate writers. An exclusive lock records hostname, PID, UID, and timestamp. A second writer receives an error unless the existing lock is stale (older than 30 minutes and the owning process is not alive on the same host). Use --break-lock on CLI commands to remove stale locks before backup, prune, forget, or check.

The server acquires an exclusive lock per active backup session (not for the entire serve lifetime), so local CLI backups can run when no remote session is in progress.

Optional durability: set sync_writes: true in config or HITSTOR_SYNC_WRITES=1 to fsync local repository files after atomic rename.

On Unix, an additional flock on locks/.exclusive guards against concurrent writers on local filesystems. The JSON lock files in locks/ remain the cross-host coordination mechanism.

min_free_reserve_bytes in config (default 1 GiB) controls the minimum free disk space required before writing new pack files on local backends.

When more than 10 index files exist, HitStor consolidates them into one and records its ID in index/latest so subsequent opens load the consolidated index first.

docs.title: Remote Backup Protocol
docs.text:
When using the remote agent (hitstor-agent), the backup pipeline is split between agent and server:

Agent responsibilities:

  • Filesystem scanning
  • Content-defined chunking (FastCDC)
  • Blob ID computation (HMAC-SHA256 with server-provided IDKey)
  • Zstd compression

Server responsibilities:

  • Deduplication verification
  • AES-256-GCM encryption
  • Pack file assembly
  • Index management
  • Snapshot creation

The IDKey is transmitted to the agent at session start, but the EncryptKey never leaves the server. See the gRPC API Reference for protocol details.

docs.title: Plugin Development Guide
docs.text: HitStor supports four plugin types via the HashiCorp go-plugin framework. Plugins run as separate processes and communicate with HitStor over gRPC.

docs.title: Plugin Types
docs.text: Type Binary Pattern Config Key Proto File Storage Backend hitstor-backend-<name> repo: plugin:<name>/args api/proto/hitstor/plugin/v1/storage.proto Notifier hitstor-notifier-<name> alert_notifier_plugins api/proto/hitstor/plugin/v1/notifier.proto Hook hitstor-hook-<name> hook_plugins api/proto/hitstor/plugin/v1/hook.proto Filesystem Scanner hitstor-scanner-<name> fs_scanner_plugin api/proto/hitstor/plugin/v1/scanner.proto

docs.title: Discovery
docs.text:
Plugins are discovered by searching for binaries matching the naming pattern:

  1. The plugin_dir config path (if set)
  2. The system $PATH

docs.title: Handshake
docs.text: All plugins use the same magic cookie handshake (HITSTOR_PLUGIN). If the handshake fails, the plugin process is killed immediately.

docs.title: Configurable Interface
docs.text: All plugin types optionally support a Configure(map[string]string) RPC, called once after launch. Implement plugin.Configurable to receive settings.

docs.title: Protocol Version
docs.text: The handshake uses ProtocolVersion: 1. Incompatible protocol changes will bump this version, causing older plugins to fail cleanly.

docs.title: Storage Backend Plugins
docs.text: Storage backend plugins provide alternative repository storage (cloud providers, databases, etc.).

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
hitstor (host)                    hitstor-backend-<name> (plugin)
     |                                    |
     |--- launch subprocess ------------->|
     |--- gRPC handshake (magic cookie) ->|
     |--- Configure(settings) ----------->|
     |--- Save/Load/Stat/Remove/List ---->|
     |--- Close() kills subprocess ------>|

docs.title: Service RPCs
docs.text: RPC Description Configure Receives plugin-specific key-value settings. Called once after launch. Save Store data under a file type and ID. Load Retrieve data for a file type and ID. Stat Return metadata (size) for a stored file. Remove Delete a stored file. List Return all IDs for a given file type.

docs.title: File Types
docs.text: Value Constant Description 0 DataFile Pack files containing encrypted chunks 1 IndexFile Index files mapping chunk IDs to pack locations 2 SnapshotFile Snapshot metadata 3 KeyFile Encryption key files 4 LockFile Repository locks 5 ConfigFile Repository configuration

docs.title: URI Scheme
docs.text:
--repo plugin:azure/myaccount/container  ->  hitstor-backend-azure
--repo plugin:gcs/my-bucket              ->  hitstor-backend-gcs

The portion after the plugin name is passed as the uri key in Configure().

docs.title: Writing a Storage Backend Plugin
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "github.com/hooperits/hitstor/internal/backend"
    hitstorplugin "github.com/hooperits/hitstor/internal/plugin"
)

type myBackend struct{}

var _ backend.Backend = (*myBackend)(nil)

// Implement Save, Load, Stat, Remove, List, Close...

func (b *myBackend) Configure(settings map[string]string) error {
    uri := settings["uri"]
    // parse uri, set up connection
    return nil
}

func main() {
    hitstorplugin.ServeStorageBackend(&myBackend{})
}

Example: See cmd/hitstor-backend-memory/main.go for a complete in-memory backend (~90 lines).

docs.title: Notifier Plugins
docs.text: Notifier plugins deliver backup event notifications to external systems (Slack, PagerDuty, email, etc.).

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
hitstor serve (host)                  hitstor-notifier-<name> (plugin)
     |                                       |
     |--- launch subprocess --------------->|
     |--- gRPC handshake (magic cookie) --->|
     |--- Configure(settings) ------------->|
     |--- Notify(event) ---- (per event) ->|
     |--- Close() kills subprocess -------->|

docs.title: Service RPCs
docs.text: RPC Description Configure Receives plugin-specific key-value settings. Called once after launch. Notify Deliver a backup event notification. Called for each event.

docs.title: Event Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description event_type string "backup_failed" or "agent_stale" server string Always "hitstor" timestamp string RFC3339 timestamp agent string Agent name that triggered the event hostname string Agent hostname (may be empty) message string Human-readable event description details map Arbitrary key-value metadata

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
hitstor config add alert_notifier_plugins slack

Both the built-in webhook notifier (alert_webhook_url) and plugin notifiers can be active simultaneously.

docs.title: Writing a Notifier Plugin
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "github.com/hooperits/hitstor/internal/notifier"
    hitstorplugin "github.com/hooperits/hitstor/internal/plugin"
)

type myNotifier struct{}

var _ notifier.Notifier = (*myNotifier)(nil)

func (n *myNotifier) Notify(ctx context.Context, event notifier.Event) error {
    // Deliver the event to your notification channel
    return nil
}

func (n *myNotifier) Close() error { return nil }

func main() {
    hitstorplugin.ServeNotifier(&myNotifier{})
}

Example: See cmd/hitstor-notifier-log/main.go for a log-based notifier plugin.

docs.title: Hook Plugins
docs.text: Hook plugins fire before and after backups, enabling custom logic such as database quiescing, cache warming, or audit logging.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
hitstor (host)                        hitstor-hook-<name> (plugin)
     |                                       |
     |--- launch subprocess --------------->|
     |--- gRPC handshake (magic cookie) --->|
     |--- Configure(settings) ------------->|
     |--- PreBackup(event) --- (before) --->|
     |--- PostBackup(event) -- (after) ---->|
     |--- Close() kills subprocess -------->|

docs.title: Service RPCs
docs.text: RPC Description Configure Receives plugin-specific key-value settings. Called once after launch. PreBackup Called before backup starts. Return an error to abort the backup. PostBackup Called after a successful backup. Errors are logged but do not fail the backup.

docs.title: Event Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description agent string Agent name performing the backup hostname string Agent hostname paths repeated string Backup source paths excludes repeated string Exclude patterns tags repeated string Backup tags snapshot_id string Snapshot ID (PostBackup only) details map Arbitrary key-value metadata

docs.title: Integration Points
docs.text:
• Server-side (hitstor serve): PreBackup fires in BeginSession() after authentication. PostBackup fires in FinalizeBackup() after snapshot creation.
  • Local backup (hitstor backup): PreBackup fires before the archiver starts. PostBackup fires after a successful backup.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: hitstor config add hook_plugins myhook

docs.title: Writing a Hook Plugin
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "github.com/hooperits/hitstor/internal/hook"
    hitstorplugin "github.com/hooperits/hitstor/internal/plugin"
)

type myHook struct{}

var _ hook.Hook = (*myHook)(nil)

func (h *myHook) PreBackup(ctx context.Context, event hook.HookEvent) error {
    // Return an error to abort the backup
    return nil
}

func (h *myHook) PostBackup(ctx context.Context, event hook.HookEvent) error {
    // event.SnapshotID contains the new snapshot ID
    return nil
}

func (h *myHook) Close() error { return nil }

func main() {
    hitstorplugin.ServeHook(&myHook{})
}

Example: See cmd/hitstor-hook-log/main.go for a log-based hook plugin.

docs.title: Filesystem Scanner Plugins
docs.text: Scanner plugins replace the built-in directory walker with custom scanning logic for cloud storage, database dumps, network shares, or custom filtering.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
hitstor (host)                        hitstor-scanner-<name> (plugin)
     |                                       |
     |--- launch subprocess --------------->|
     |--- gRPC handshake (magic cookie) --->|
     |--- Configure(settings) ------------->|
     |--- Scan(paths, excludes) ----------->|
     |<-- stream ScanEntry (per file) ------|
     |--- Close() kills subprocess -------->|

The Scan RPC uses server-side streaming -- the plugin sends one ScanEntry per file/directory.

docs.title: Service RPCs
docs.text: RPC Description Configure Receives plugin-specific key-value settings. Called once after launch. Scan Walks paths and streams file/directory entries back to the host.

docs.title: ScanEntry Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description path string Absolute path of the file or directory node NodeInfo File metadata error_message string Non-fatal error for this entry

docs.title: NodeInfo Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description name string Base name type string "file", "dir", or "symlink" mode uint32 Unix file mode bits uid uint32 Owner user ID gid uint32 Owner group ID mtime_ns int64 Modification time (nanoseconds since epoch) atime_ns int64 Access time (nanoseconds since epoch) ctime_ns int64 Change time (nanoseconds since epoch) size uint64 File size in bytes inode uint64 Inode number links uint64 Hard link count link_target string Symlink target path

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
# Only one scanner plugin active at a time
hitstor config set fs_scanner_plugin myscanner

docs.title: Writing a Scanner Plugin
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "github.com/hooperits/hitstor/internal/scanner"
    hitstorplugin "github.com/hooperits/hitstor/internal/plugin"
)

type myScanner struct{}

var _ scanner.Scanner = (*myScanner)(nil)

func (s *myScanner) Scan(paths []string, excludes []string) (<-chan scanner.ScanResult, error) {
    ch := make(chan scanner.ScanResult)
    go func() {
        defer close(ch)
        // Walk paths and send results on the channel
    }()
    return ch, nil
}

func (s *myScanner) Close() error { return nil }

func main() {
    hitstorplugin.ServeFilesystemScanner(&myScanner{})
}

Example: See cmd/hitstor-scanner-builtin/main.go for a scanner plugin that wraps the built-in walker.

docs.title: Unit Tests
docs.text:
Test your interface implementation directly without launching a subprocess:

be := &myBackend{}
be.Configure(map[string]string{"uri": "test"})
be.Save(ctx, backend.DataFile, id, data)
// ...

docs.title: Integration Tests
docs.text:
Build the plugin binary, then launch it via the plugin manager:

be, err := plugin.OpenStorageBackend("mycloud", "/path/to/bin", map[string]string{
    "uri": "test-bucket",
})
defer be.Close()

See internal/plugin/integration_test.go for working examples of all four plugin types.

docs.title: Message Size Limits
docs.text: go-plugin sets max gRPC message size to ~2 GiB. HitStor pack files cap at 128 MiB, so no streaming is needed for storage backends. The filesystem scanner plugin uses server-side streaming for large directory trees.

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• Plugin Usage Guide -- installing and configuring plugins
  • API Reference -- main gRPC backup protocol

docs.title: Agent Commands
docs.text: Reference for all hitstor-agent CLI commands.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command Description backup Send a backup to the remote server ping Test connectivity to the server daemon Run as a long-lived daemon with management server and backup polling show-id Display the agent token for dashboard registration service Manage the Windows Service (Windows only)

docs.title: Global Flags
docs.text: Flag Type Default Description --server string Remote server address (host:port) --api-key string Agent API key for authentication --ca-cert string Path to CA certificate for TLS verification --hostname string system hostname Override hostname sent to server --config string Path to config file

docs.title: hitstor-agent backup
docs.text: Send a backup to the remote server.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: hitstor-agent backup [flags] [paths...]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Scans the given paths, splits files into content-defined chunks (FastCDC), compresses each chunk with Zstd, and uploads new chunks to the remote HitStor server over gRPC/TLS. The server handles deduplication, encryption, and storage.

At least one path argument is required (or configured via agent_paths).

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Type Default Description --exclude string Exclude files matching this glob pattern (repeatable)

Plus all agent global flags.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Back up specific directories:

hitstor-agent backup --server backup.internal:8420 \
  --api-key YOUR_KEY /etc /home /var/lib

Using environment variables:

export HITSTOR_AGENT_SERVER=backup.internal:8420
export HITSTOR_AGENT_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY
hitstor-agent backup /etc /home

Using config file paths:

hitstor-agent backup

docs.title: hitstor-agent bmr
docs.text: Build and inspect bare-metal recovery media.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
hitstor-agent bmr check [flags]
hitstor-agent bmr generate-config [flags]
hitstor-agent bmr build-media [flags]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Identical command tree to hitstor bmr — both binaries share the same implementation, since recovery media can only be built on the host it protects, and hitstor-agent is what actually ships on a protected host.

One difference: on hitstor-agent, the --server flag's default value is pre-filled from the agent's own configured server address (the one it normally reports backups to), so generate-config/build-media need less to be typed on a machine that is already a registered agent. On hitstor, --server has no default.

See hitstor bmr for the full flag reference, subcommand descriptions, and examples — they apply here unchanged.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Recovery itself is driven by hitstor-agent recover, invoked automatically from the rescue media.
  • See Bare-metal restore for the full workflow.

docs.title: hitstor-agent daemon
docs.text: Run as a long-lived daemon with management server and backup polling.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: hitstor-agent daemon [flags]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Runs the agent as a long-lived process with two functions:

  1. Management server — listens on a gRPC port (default: 8422) for commands from the HitStor server, including registration, filesystem browsing, and configuration
  2. Backup polling — periodically polls the server for a backup schedule and runs backups when due

The daemon starts in one of two modes:

  • Unconfigured (new install): Only runs the management server. Logs "waiting for registration from dashboard." When the server registers the agent via the dashboard, the daemon transitions to configured mode automatically.
  • Configured (after registration or legacy install): Runs both the management server and the backup polling loop.

Graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM (Linux) or service stop (Windows).

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Flag Type Default Description --listen-port int 8422 gRPC listen port for server management connections --poll-interval duration 5m How often to check the server for schedule updates

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Run in foreground (dashboard-managed):

hitstor-agent daemon --listen-port 8422

Run in foreground (legacy mode):

hitstor-agent daemon --server backup.internal:8420 --api-key YOUR_KEY

Run via systemd:

sudo systemctl enable --now hitstor-agent

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Description HITSTOR_AGENT_LISTEN_PORT Override the default listen port (8422)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• On first start, the daemon generates an agent token at /etc/hitstor/agent-token if one does not exist
  • The management server uses self-signed TLS (auto-generated)
  • If no schedule is configured, the daemon polls every 5 minutes and logs a message
  • Alternative to daemon mode: use systemd timers with hitstor-agent backup for cron-style scheduling

docs.title: hitstor-agent ping
docs.text: Test connectivity to the server.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: hitstor-agent ping [flags]

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Sends a gRPC Ping request to the remote server to verify connectivity, TLS certificate validation, and API key authentication. Prints the server version on success.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
hitstor-agent ping --server backup.internal:8420 --api-key YOUR_KEY

Successful output:

pong: server v0.1.0

docs.title: hitstor-agent recover
docs.text: Run in bare-metal recovery mode (invoked from rescue media).

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: hitstor-agent recover --token TOKEN [flags]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Recovery mode is what the rescue system runs after ReaR has recreated the machine's disk layout and mounted the new root.

It is not a normal agent: it starts no schedule, writes no configuration, and exits as soon as the restore it is here for reaches a terminal state.

Every other restore in HitStor is started by the server dialling an agent it already knows the address of. A machine that just booted off rescue media has whatever address DHCP handed it, which nobody has told the server about — so this calls home instead, presenting a single-use recovery token, and the server dials back over the ordinary restore path.

ReaR installs a bootloader only if this command exits 0.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Type Default Description --token string Required. Single-use recovery token, issued from the dashboard (Disaster Recovery → Bare Metal) --agent string this host's hostname Registered agent name being recovered --target string /mnt/local Directory the recreated root is mounted on --listen-port int 8422 gRPC port for the server to push the restore to --timeout duration 12h Give up if no restore completes within this window

Plus --server and --ca-cert from the agent's global flags.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: hitstor-agent recover --token abc123... --server backup.internal:8420

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Refuses to run if --target is not an existing directory — this catches the case where ReaR did not actually mount the recreated root, which would otherwise make the restore silently write into the rescue system's ramdisk and vanish at reboot.
  • The listener authenticates on a token generated for this recovery run; the original agent's token lived on the disk that no longer exists.
  • Non-fatal per-file restore errors are reported as warnings after the restore completes rather than failing the command, since the exit code gates whether ReaR installs a bootloader — review them before rebooting.
  • See Bare-metal restore for the full recovery workflow and how the recovery token is issued.

docs.title: hitstor-agent service
docs.text: Manage the Windows Service (Windows only).

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
hitstor-agent service install
hitstor-agent service start
hitstor-agent service stop
hitstor-agent service uninstall

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Manages the HitStor Agent as a Windows Service. The service runs in daemon mode, polling the server for scheduled backups.

docs.title: service install
docs.text: Register the agent as a Windows Service. Requires administrator privileges.

docs.title: service start
docs.text: Start the Windows Service.

docs.title: service stop
docs.text: Stop the Windows Service.

docs.title: service uninstall
docs.text: Remove the Windows Service registration.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Install and start the service:

hitstor-agent service install
hitstor-agent service start

Check service status:

Get-Service HitStorAgent

Stop and uninstall:

hitstor-agent service stop
hitstor-agent service uninstall

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The service runs as LocalSystem by default.
  • Configuration is read from %AppData%\hitstor\config.yaml or environment variables.
  • Service logs are written to the Windows Event Log.
  • This command is a no-op on Linux (Linux uses systemd instead).

docs.title: hitstor-agent show-id
docs.text: Display the agent token for dashboard registration.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: hitstor-agent show-id

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Reads and prints the agent token from /etc/hitstor/agent-token. The token is a 64-character hexadecimal string generated during agent installation or on first daemon start.

Use this token when adding the agent from the HitStor dashboard:

  1. Open the dashboard and navigate to Agents
  2. Click + Add Agent
  3. Enter the agent's IP address, port (default: 8422), and this token

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
sudo hitstor-agent show-id

Output:

a3f8c1d9e4b72a5601df83be9c7f4a2d0e6b1893fc5d74a0e2c8f961b3d507ea

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The token file is located at /etc/hitstor/agent-token with mode 0600 (root-only readable)
  • If the token file does not exist, start the agent daemon first (hitstor-agent daemon) — it generates the token automatically
  • The token is used by the server to authenticate management gRPC calls (filesystem browsing, configuration)

docs.title: Server Commands
docs.text: Reference for all hitstor CLI commands.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command Description init Initialize a new backup repository backup Back up files to the repository restore Restore files from a snapshot snapshots List all snapshots (alias: ls) forget Remove snapshots by ID or retention policy prune Remove unreferenced data from the repository check Verify repository integrity serve Start the gRPC backup server config Manage configuration diff Compare two snapshots du Show repository disk usage repo Repository operations (multi-repo aware) jobs Manage scheduled backup jobs agents Manage registered backup agents version Display version information

docs.title: Global Flags
docs.text: Flag Type Default Description --repo string Repository location (path or s3:endpoint/bucket) — legacy single-repo --repo-name string Select repository by name from multi-repo config (preferred) --config string ~/.config/hitstor/config.yaml Path to config file (on servers often /etc/hitstor/config.yaml) --password string Repository password --password-file string Path to file containing the repository password --parallel int 0 Number of parallel workers (0 = auto-detect, max 8) --s3-access-key string S3 access key --s3-secret-key string S3 secret key --s3-region string us-east-1 S3 region --json bool false Output in JSON format (where supported) --no-color bool false Disable colored output

docs.title: hitstor agents
docs.text: Manage registered backup agents (multi-repo aware).

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: hitstor agents [command]

docs.title: Available Commands
docs.text: Command Description add Register a new backup agent (supports --addr for managed) list List registered backup agents (supports --repo-name, --all-repos, --json) remove Remove a registered backup agent assign-repo Assign target repo for an agent (for future jobs)

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Agents perform backups. In multi-repo setups, use --repo-name to target a specific repository's agent registry.

Supports both simple and dashboard-managed agents.

Service management is available on the agent binary (hitstor-agent service ... on both Linux and Windows).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
hitstor --config /etc/hitstor/config.yaml --repo-name Production agents list
hitstor --config /etc/hitstor/config.yaml agents add --addr 192.168.1.10:8422 my-agent
hitstor --config /etc/hitstor/config.yaml agents assign-repo my-agent Production
hitstor --config /etc/hitstor/config.yaml agents list --all-repos

See also: hitstor jobs (jobs reference agents), dashboard agent management, and hitstor-agent service.

docs.title: hitstor backup
docs.text: Back up files to the repository.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: hitstor backup [flags] [paths...]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Scans the given paths, splits files into content-defined chunks (FastCDC), deduplicates against existing repository data and a local SQLite cache, compresses (Zstd), encrypts (AES-256-GCM), and writes the data to the repository as pack files. A snapshot is created recording the backed-up paths, hostname, timestamp, and tree structure.

At least one path argument is required.

An exclusive lock is acquired on the repository for the duration of the backup.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Type Default Description --exclude string Exclude files matching this glob pattern (repeatable) --tag string Add a tag to the snapshot (repeatable) --host string system hostname Override the hostname stored in the snapshot --dry-run bool false Preview what would be backed up without writing data

Plus all global flags, including --repo-name for multi-repo setups.

docs.title: Exclude Merging
docs.text: --exclude patterns are merged with any exclude patterns defined in the config file. Both sources apply during the backup.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Back up a single directory:

hitstor backup --repo /backups/hitstor --password "secret" /home/user/documents

# Using named repo from multi-repo config
hitstor --config /etc/hitstor/config.yaml --repo-name Production backup /data

Back up multiple paths with exclusions:

hitstor backup --repo /backups/hitstor --password "secret" \
  /home/user/documents /home/user/photos \
  --exclude "*.tmp" --exclude ".cache/**"

Tag a backup for identification:

hitstor backup --repo /backups/hitstor --password "secret" /data \
  --tag "pre-upgrade" --tag "production"

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Files that change during the backup (detected by re-checking mtime/size after reading) are skipped with a warning.
  • Unchanged files are detected via the SQLite files cache and their chunks are not re-read from disk.
  • Paths are resolved to absolute paths before being stored in the snapshot.

docs.title: hitstor bmr
docs.text: Build and inspect bare-metal recovery media.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
hitstor bmr check [flags]
hitstor bmr generate-config [flags]
hitstor bmr build-media [flags]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Bare-metal recovery media lets a machine with a blank disk boot, recreate its disk layout, and pull its data back from HitStor.

These commands run on the protected host itself: the image embeds that host's kernel, drivers, and disk layout, so it cannot be produced from a backup alone. Building media is a deliberate action, not something a backup does for you — run it after the host's storage layout changes.

Linux only; HitStor drives Relax-and-Recover (ReaR) underneath.

The same command tree is available as hitstor-agent bmr — see hitstor-agent bmr for the one behavioral difference.

docs.title: check
docs.text:
Reports everything standing between this host and a bootable rescue image: whether ReaR is installed and which version, which supporting tools are present, and whether the command has the privileges ReaR needs.

Reports every gap at once rather than stopping at the first, and exits non-zero when the host is not ready, so it can gate a provisioning script.

hitstor bmr check

docs.title: generate-config
docs.text:
Writes /etc/rear/local.conf and the EXTERNAL_RESTORE hook the rescue system runs once it has recreated the disk layout.

No credentials are written: the recovery token and, where needed, the repository password are prompted for at recovery time, so the media can be stored without becoming a way into the repository.

build-media regenerates both files, so running this separately is only needed to review or hand-edit them first.

hitstor bmr generate-config --server backup.internal:8420 --agent web-01
Flag Type Default Description --stdout bool false Print the configuration instead of writing it

Plus the shared media flags below.

docs.title: build-media
docs.text:
Runs ReaR to produce a bootable rescue image for this host, after writing the configuration that points its recovery run back at HitStor.

The build takes several minutes and reads every disk on the machine, so it is deliberately manual. Rebuild it whenever the host's disk layout changes — a stale image recreates the old layout.

hitstor bmr build-media --server backup.internal:8420 --agent web-01
Flag Type Default Description --force bool false Build even when the readiness check reports blockers

Plus the shared media flags below.

docs.title: Shared media flags
docs.text:
generate-config and build-media both take:

Flag Type Default Description --output-dir string /var/lib/hitstor/bmr Directory ReaR writes the finished ISO into --agent-binary string /usr/bin/hitstor-agent hitstor-agent binary to embed in the rescue image --hook-script string /usr/share/hitstor/bmr/hitstor-recover.sh Path to write the ReaR EXTERNAL_RESTORE hook to --config-path string /etc/rear/local.conf Path to write the generated ReaR configuration to --server string HitStor server address to prefill in the recovery prompt (host:port) --agent string Registered agent name to prefill in the recovery prompt --migration-mode bool false Allow recovery onto dissimilar hardware or a virtual machine (ReaR MIGRATION_MODE) --copy stringArray Additional absolute path to embed in the rescue image (repeatable)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• check, generate-config, and build-media all support the global --json flag for machine-readable output.
  • Recovery itself is driven by hitstor-agent recover, invoked automatically from the rescue media once ReaR has recreated the disk layout — see hitstor-agent recover.
  • See Bare-metal restore for the full workflow, including what the recovery media does and does not capture.

docs.title: hitstor check
docs.text: Verify repository integrity.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: hitstor check [flags]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Checks the structural integrity of the repository. By default, it verifies that all snapshots, indexes, and pack metadata are consistent and readable.

With --read-data, it additionally reads and decrypts every blob in every pack file, verifying that no data is corrupted. This is slower but provides a thorough end-to-end verification.

Errors are printed to stderr. The exit code is non-zero if any errors are found.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Type Default Description --read-data bool false Read and verify all pack data (slower but thorough)

Plus all global flags, including --repo-name for multi-repo setups.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Quick structural check:

hitstor check --repo /backups/hitstor --password "secret"

Full verification including all blob data:

hitstor check --repo /backups/hitstor --password "secret" --read-data

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Without --read-data, the check verifies metadata consistency (snapshots reference valid trees, indexes are well-formed, etc.) but does not read pack file contents.
  • With --read-data, every blob is decrypted and its ID is re-verified. This catches bit-rot, truncated files, and other storage-level corruption.

docs.title: hitstor config
docs.text: Manage configuration.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
hitstor config show [--json]
hitstor config set <key> <value>
hitstor config unset <key>
hitstor config add <key> <value>
hitstor config remove <key> <value>
hitstor config init
hitstor config edit
hitstor config path
hitstor config repositories list

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Manage the HitStor configuration file at ~/.config/hitstor/config.yaml (or /etc/hitstor/config.yaml on servers with --config).

For modern multi-repo management (repositories list, S3 creds, etc.), prefer the hitstor repo subcommand. The legacy flat keys here are for backward compat.

Configuration values can be set, unset, or viewed. List-type keys support add and remove operations.

docs.title: config show
docs.text: Display all configuration keys with their effective values and sources (default, config, env, flag). Sensitive values are masked. Use --json for machine-readable output.

docs.title: config set <key> <value>
docs.text: Set a configuration key to a value. The value is validated before saving.

docs.title: config unset <key>
docs.text: Remove a configuration key, reverting to its default value.

docs.title: config add <key> <value>
docs.text: Append a value to a list-type key (e.g., exclude, agent_paths).

docs.title: config remove <key> <value>
docs.text: Remove a specific value from a list-type key.

docs.title: config init
docs.text: Interactive setup wizard. Walks through essential configuration options with prompts and examples.

docs.title: config edit
docs.text: Open the configuration file in your default editor ($EDITOR).

docs.title: config path
docs.text: Print the path to the configuration file. Prefers system /etc/hitstor/config.yaml on servers when present and readable.

docs.title: config repositories list
docs.text: List modern repositories from config (equivalent to hitstor repo list). For management, use the repo subcommands.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Show all config values:

hitstor config show

Set the repository location:

hitstor config set repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo

Add an exclude pattern:

hitstor config add exclude "*.tmp"

Run the interactive setup:

hitstor config init

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Configuration file uses YAML format.
  • Precedence: CLI flags > environment variables > config file > defaults.
  • See Config Reference for the full list of keys.

docs.title: hitstor diff
docs.text: Compare two snapshots.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: hitstor diff [flags] <snapshot-id-1> <snapshot-id-2>

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Compares two snapshots and displays the differences between them. Shows files that were added, removed, or modified between the two snapshots.

Both snapshot IDs are required and can be specified as full IDs, short prefixes, or latest.

Supports --repo-name for multi-repo (see global flags in index.md).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Compare two snapshots:

hitstor diff --repo /backups/hitstor --password "secret" a1b2c3d4 b5c6d7e8

Compare a specific snapshot with the latest:

hitstor diff --repo /backups/hitstor --password "secret" a1b2c3d4 latest

docs.title: hitstor du
docs.text: Show repository disk usage.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: hitstor du [flags]

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Displays the disk usage of the repository, showing the total size of pack files, index files, snapshot files, and the overall total.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Show disk usage:

hitstor du --repo /backups/hitstor --password "secret"

docs.title: hitstor forget
docs.text: Remove snapshots by ID or retention policy.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: hitstor forget [flags] [snapshot-id...]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Removes snapshots from the repository. There are two modes of operation:

  • Explicit IDs — pass one or more snapshot IDs (full or prefix) as arguments to remove those specific snapshots.
  • Retention policy — use --keep-* flags to automatically determine which snapshots to keep and which to forget.

These two modes cannot be combined. Providing both snapshot IDs and --keep-* flags is an error.

Forgetting a snapshot removes only the snapshot metadata. The actual data packs remain on disk until prune is run. Use --prune to automatically run prune after forgetting.

An exclusive lock is acquired on the repository for the duration of the operation.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Type Default Description --keep-last int 0 Keep the N most recent snapshots --keep-hourly int 0 Keep N hourly snapshots --keep-daily int 0 Keep N daily snapshots --keep-weekly int 0 Keep N weekly snapshots --keep-monthly int 0 Keep N monthly snapshots --keep-yearly int 0 Keep N yearly snapshots --keep-tag string Keep snapshots with this tag (repeatable) --host string Only apply policy to snapshots from this host --path string Only apply policy to snapshots with this path --dry-run bool false Only show what would be removed --prune bool false Run prune after forgetting to reclaim space

Plus all global flags, including --repo-name for multi-repo setups.

docs.title: Retention Semantics
docs.text:
Retention flags use union semantics: a snapshot is kept if it matches any of the active --keep-* rules. For example, with --keep-last 3 --keep-daily 7, a snapshot is kept if it is among the 3 most recent or among the 7 most recent daily snapshots.

The --host and --path flags filter which snapshots the policy applies to. Snapshots not matching the filter are left untouched.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Forget a specific snapshot:

hitstor forget --repo /backups/hitstor --password "secret" a1b2c3d4

Apply a retention policy:

hitstor forget --repo /backups/hitstor --password "secret" \
  --keep-last 5 --keep-daily 7 --keep-weekly 4 --keep-monthly 12

Preview what would be removed:

hitstor forget --repo /backups/hitstor --password "secret" \
  --keep-last 3 --dry-run

Forget and prune in one step:

hitstor forget --repo /backups/hitstor --password "secret" \
  --keep-last 5 --prune

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• After forgetting snapshots without --prune, HitStor prints a reminder to run hitstor prune.
  • --keep-tag keeps any snapshot that has the specified tag, regardless of other retention rules.

docs.title: hitstor init
docs.text: Initialize a new backup repository.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: hitstor init [flags]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Creates a new encrypted backup repository at the location specified by --repo. This sets up the directory structure (data/, index/, snapshots/, keys/, locks/, config) and generates a master key encrypted with the provided password using scrypt key derivation.

The repository must not already exist. The repository ID is printed on success.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: This command uses only the global flags.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Initialize a local repository:

hitstor init --repo /backups/hitstor --password "my-secret-password"

Initialize an S3 repository:

hitstor init \
  --repo s3:http://localhost:9000/hitstor-backups \
  --password "my-secret-password" \
  --s3-access-key minioadmin \
  --s3-secret-key minioadmin

Using environment variables:

export HITSTOR_REPO=/backups/hitstor
export HITSTOR_PASSWORD="my-secret-password"
hitstor init

docs.title: hitstor jobs
docs.text:
Manage scheduled backup jobs (multi-repo aware).

Note: Full job CRUD, scheduling, and execution is primarily performed via the dashboard. The CLI currently provides basic support and will be expanded.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: hitstor jobs [command]

docs.title: Subcommands
docs.text: Command Description list List configured backup jobs create Define a new backup job (currently prints definition; full persistence coming)

docs.title: Flags for create
docs.text:
• --name (required)
  • --repo-name (required)
  • --job-type (only files is supported)
  • --path (repeatable)
  • --interval-hours, --cron, --timezone, --agent-name

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
hitstor --config /etc/hitstor/config.yaml jobs list

hitstor --config /etc/hitstor/config.yaml jobs create \
  --name "Daily /home" \
  --repo-name Production \
  --job-type files \
  --path /home \
  --interval-hours 24

For production job management use the dashboard Storage + Jobs pages.

docs.title: hitstor prune
docs.text: Remove unreferenced data from the repository.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: hitstor prune [flags]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Removes pack files, index entries, and blobs that are no longer referenced by any snapshot. Run this after forget to reclaim storage space.

Prune performs a mark-and-sweep garbage collection:

  1. Scans all snapshots to determine which blobs are still referenced.
  2. Identifies pack files containing only unreferenced blobs (deleted entirely) or a mix of referenced and unreferenced blobs (repacked).
  3. Writes new pack files containing only the referenced blobs from mixed packs.
  4. Deletes obsolete pack files and updates indexes.

An exclusive lock is acquired on the repository for the duration of the operation.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Type Default Description --dry-run bool false Only show what would be removed --max-repack-size string Limit total bytes repacked (e.g., 500MiB, 2GiB)

Plus all global flags, including --repo-name for multi-repo setups.

docs.title: Size Suffixes
docs.text:
Suffix Meaning B Bytes KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB Binary units (1024-based) KB, MB, GB, TB Decimal units (1000-based)

If no suffix is given, the value is treated as bytes.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Prune unreferenced data:

hitstor prune --repo /backups/hitstor --password "secret"

Preview what would be removed:

hitstor prune --repo /backups/hitstor --password "secret" --dry-run

Limit repacking to 500 MiB:

hitstor prune --repo /backups/hitstor --password "secret" --max-repack-size 500MiB

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Prune is also available as part of forget --prune, which combines both operations.
  • The operation reports the number of packs deleted, packs repacked, bytes freed, and indexes updated.

docs.title: hitstor repo
docs.text: Repository management commands (multi-repository aware).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: hitstor repo [command]

docs.title: Subcommands
docs.text: Command Description list List configured repositories from the multi-repo config create <name> <path> Create and initialize a new local repository delete <name> Remove a repository from the config (does not delete data) health Show operational health for the selected repository

docs.title: Global Flags (relevant)
docs.text:
• --repo-name <name> — Select a named repository from the repositories: list in config.
  • --config /etc/hitstor/config.yaml — Recommended when running on the server.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# List all repositories known to this server
hitstor --config /etc/hitstor/config.yaml repo list

# Create a new local repo (creates password file next to config)
hitstor --config /etc/hitstor/config.yaml repo create MyRepo /data/myrepo

# Health check on a named repo
hitstor --config /etc/hitstor/config.yaml --repo-name MyRepo repo health

See also: hitstor config show (shows modern repositories section when present).

docs.title: hitstor restore
docs.text: Restore files from a snapshot.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: hitstor restore [flags] <snapshot-id> <target-path>

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Restores all files from the specified snapshot to the target directory. The snapshot can be identified by its full 64-character hex ID, a unique short prefix, or the keyword latest (which resolves to the most recent snapshot by timestamp).

Both arguments are required: the snapshot ID and the target path where files will be written.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Type Default Description --include string Restore only files matching this path (repeatable)

Plus all global flags, including --repo-name for multi-repo setups.

docs.title: Snapshot ID Resolution
docs.text:
HitStor supports three ways to identify a snapshot:

  • Full ID — the complete 64-character hex string
  • Short prefix — a unique prefix of the snapshot ID (e.g., a1b2c3d4). If the prefix is ambiguous (matches multiple snapshots), an error is returned.
  • latest — resolves to the snapshot with the most recent timestamp

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Restore the latest snapshot:

hitstor restore --repo /backups/hitstor --password "secret" latest /tmp/restore

Restore a specific snapshot by short ID:

hitstor restore --repo /backups/hitstor --password "secret" a1b2c3d4 /tmp/restore

Restore only specific files:

hitstor restore --repo /backups/hitstor --password "secret" latest /tmp/restore \
  --include "/home/user/documents/important.pdf"

docs.title: hitstor serve
docs.text: Start the gRPC backup server.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
hitstor serve [flags]
hitstor serve agent add <name>
hitstor serve agent list
hitstor serve agent remove <name>

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Starts the HitStor gRPC server that accepts remote agent backups over TLS. The server handles deduplication, encryption, and storage on behalf of remote agents. It also starts the web dashboard on a separate HTTP port.

If no TLS certificate is provided, a self-signed certificate is generated automatically.

An exclusive lock is acquired on the repository for the duration of the server lifetime.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Type Default Description --port int 8420 gRPC listen port --tls-cert string Path to TLS certificate file --tls-key string Path to TLS private key file --dashboard-port int 8421 HTTP dashboard listen port

Plus all global flags.

docs.title: serve agent add <name>
docs.text: Register a new backup agent. Outputs a 64-character hex API key that the agent uses for authentication. Save this key immediately — it cannot be displayed again.

docs.title: serve agent list
docs.text: List all registered agents with their names, creation dates, and last backup times.

docs.title: serve agent remove <name>
docs.text: Remove a registered agent. The agent will no longer be able to connect.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Start the server with default settings:

hitstor serve --repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo --password "secret"

Start with custom TLS certificates:

hitstor serve --repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo --password "secret" \
  --tls-cert /etc/hitstor/tls/server.crt \
  --tls-key /etc/hitstor/tls/server.key

Register a new agent:

hitstor serve agent add webserver-01 \
  --repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo --password "secret"

List registered agents:

hitstor serve agent list \
  --repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo --password "secret"

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The server requires a local filesystem backend (not S3) because the agent registry is stored alongside the repository.
  • Graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM.
  • The dashboard is served as an embedded HTML5 application with no external dependencies.

docs.title: hitstor snapshots
docs.text: List all snapshots in the repository.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: hitstor snapshots [flags]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Lists all snapshots stored in the repository, sorted by time (newest first). By default, output is a formatted table showing each snapshot's short ID, timestamp, hostname, paths, file count, and total size.

Use --json for machine-readable JSON output.

Alias: hitstor ls

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Type Default Description --host string Show only snapshots from this hostname --path string Show only snapshots that include this backed-up path

Plus all global flags, including --repo-name to target a specific repository in multi-repo setups.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
List all snapshots:

hitstor snapshots --repo /backups/hitstor --password "secret"

Filter by hostname:

hitstor snapshots --repo /backups/hitstor --password "secret" --host webserver-01

JSON output:

hitstor snapshots --repo /backups/hitstor --password "secret" --json

docs.title: Table (default)
docs.text:
ID         Time                 Host         Paths                   Files       Size
a1b2c3d4   2025-01-15 10:30:00  myhost       /home/user/documents      150     45 MiB
b5c6d7e8   2025-01-14 10:30:00  myhost       /home/user/documents      148     44 MiB

docs.title: JSON (--json)
docs.text:
[
  {
    "id": "a1b2c3d4",
    "time": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z",
    "hostname": "myhost",
    "paths": ["/home/user/documents"],
    "total_files": 150,
    "total_size": 47185920
  }
]

docs.title: hitstor verify-restore
docs.text: Test-restore a snapshot and re-hash files (restore verification).

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: hitstor verify-restore <snapshot-id> [flags]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Restores a snapshot (or a sample of its files) to a temporary directory, re-chunks each restored file with the repository chunker, and compares content blob IDs to the snapshot tree.

This is the primary trust signal that a filesystem backup is actually restorable — it round-trips real data through restore and re-chunking rather than just checking metadata.

Use latest as the snapshot ID to verify the most recent snapshot. Tab completion for snapshot IDs is available.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Type Default Description --max-files int 0 (all) Limit the number of files verified --max-bytes uint64 0 (unlimited) Limit total bytes verified --keep-temp bool false Keep the temporary restore directory instead of cleaning it up

Plus all global flags, including --repo-name for multi-repo setups.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Verify the latest snapshot in full:

hitstor verify-restore latest --repo /backups/hitstor --password "secret"

Sample-verify a large snapshot, capping at 500 files:

hitstor verify-restore a1b2c3d4 --max-files 500

Verify and keep the temp restore for manual inspection:

hitstor verify-restore latest --keep-temp

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Every backup job's dashboard entry can also run this automatically after each backup — see Guided disaster recovery.
  • A non-zero exit code means either a mismatch was found or the verification itself errored; mismatches are printed to stderr with the mismatched path and reason.
  • With --json, output is a single JSON object (ok, snapshot_id, files_checked, files_sampled, bytes_checked, symlinks_ok, sampled, duration, mismatches, error, restore_target) instead of the human-readable summary.

docs.title: hitstor version
docs.text: Display version information and check for updates.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: hitstor version [--check] [--json]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Prints the HitStor version, commit hash, build date, and platform.

With --check, contacts the GitHub Releases API to determine if a newer version is available.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Flag Description --check Check for available updates --json Output in JSON format

docs.title: Print version
docs.text:
hitstor version

Output:

hitstor v1.0.0 (commit a1b2c3d, built 2026-02-27, linux/amd64)

docs.title: Check for updates
docs.text:
hitstor version --check

Output when an update is available:

Update available: v1.1.0 (current: v1.0.0)
Release: https://github.com/hooperits/hitstor/releases/tag/v1.1.0

Output when up to date:

You are running the latest version (v1.0.0).

Output when the check fails (network error):

Could not check for updates.

docs.title: Automatic Version Check
docs.text:
When update_check: true is set in the server configuration (the default), the server checks for updates every 24 hours. If a newer version is available, a notification banner appears at the top of the web dashboard.

See Configuration Reference for the update_check and update_url settings.

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text: The HitStor User Guide covers everything you need to know to protect your data with encrypted, deduplicated backups. Whether you are backing up a single laptop or managing retention policies across multiple servers, this guide walks you through every step.

docs.title: Topics
docs.text: Guide Description Getting Started End-to-end tutorial that takes you from initializing a repository to restoring files. Backup Create backups, exclude files, use tags, tune parallelism, and understand deduplication. Restore Restore full snapshots or individual files, resolve snapshot IDs, and verify restored data. Snapshots List, filter, compare, and inspect snapshots stored in your repository. Retention Define retention policies, remove old snapshots with forget, and reclaim space with prune. Configuration Manage the config file, environment variables, and interactive setup wizard. Plugins Discover, install, and configure storage backends, notifiers, hooks, and scanner plugins.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Before following the guides in this section, make sure you have HitStor installed. See the Installation Guide for platform-specific instructions.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
Throughout the User Guide the following conventions are used:

  • Commands prefixed with $ are run in a terminal.
  • Text in UPPER_CASE (such as SNAPSHOT_ID) represents a value you must replace with your own.
  • Optional flags are shown in square brackets: [--flag VALUE].
  • Long commands are split across multiple lines with \ for readability.

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: The hitstor backup command creates a new snapshot of one or more directories. Each snapshot captures the full state of the specified paths at the time the backup runs, but thanks to content-defined chunking and deduplication, only new or changed data is actually written to the repository.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
hitstor backup --repo /path/to/repo --password "secret" /path/to/backup

This creates a snapshot containing every file under /path/to/backup.

docs.title: Backing Up Multiple Paths
docs.text:
You can specify more than one source path in a single backup:

hitstor backup --repo /path/to/repo --password "secret" \
    /home/user/documents \
    /home/user/photos \
    /etc

All listed paths are included in the same snapshot.

docs.title: Command-Line Excludes
docs.text:
Use --exclude to skip files or directories that match a pattern:

hitstor backup --repo /path/to/repo --password "secret" \
    --exclude "*.tmp" \
    --exclude "node_modules" \
    /home/user/projects

Patterns follow standard glob syntax:

Pattern Matches *.log All files ending in .log cache/ Any directory named cache /data/temp The exact path /data/temp relative to the backup root **/build A directory named build at any depth

docs.title: Config File Excludes
docs.text:
You can also define excludes in the configuration file (~/.config/hitstor/config.yaml):

backup:
  exclude:
    - "*.tmp"
    - ".cache"
    - "node_modules"

docs.title: Merging Behavior
docs.text: Excludes from both sources are merged at runtime. A file is excluded if it matches any pattern from either the command line or the config file. Command-line patterns do not replace config-file patterns; they add to them.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
Tags let you label snapshots for easier filtering later. Use --tag (repeatable) to attach one or more tags:

hitstor backup --repo /path/to/repo --password "secret" \
    --tag project-alpha \
    --tag weekly \
    /data/project-alpha

Tags appear in the hitstor snapshots output and can be used with --keep-tag in retention policies. See Retention for details.

docs.title: Host Override
docs.text:
By default HitStor records the system hostname in each snapshot. If you back up the same data from multiple machines, or if your hostname changes, you can override it:

hitstor backup --repo /path/to/repo --password "secret" \
    --host webserver-01 \
    /var/www

The host value is used by forget when applying per-host retention policies.

docs.title: Dry Run Mode
docs.text:
To preview what a backup would do without writing any data, pass --dry-run:

hitstor backup --repo /path/to/repo --password "secret" \
    --dry-run \
    /data

The command scans the source paths, reports file counts and estimated data sizes, but does not create a snapshot or write any packs.

docs.title: Parallel Workers
docs.text:
HitStor processes files concurrently. The --parallel flag controls the number of worker goroutines:

hitstor backup --repo /path/to/repo --password "secret" \
    --parallel 4 \
    /data

The default behavior auto-detects the number of CPUs and caps at 8 workers. On I/O-bound workloads (network storage, spinning disks) you may get better throughput with fewer workers; on fast SSDs you can try increasing the count.

Situation Recommended --parallel NVMe SSD, many small files 6--8 Spinning disk 1--2 Network mount (NFS, SMB) 2--4 S3 backend 4--8

docs.title: Progress Display
docs.text:
While the backup runs, HitStor prints a live progress line showing:

  • Number of files scanned
  • Amount of data processed
  • Amount of new data added to the repository
  • Elapsed time and estimated time remaining

The progress display updates in place on terminals that support carriage returns. When the output is redirected to a file or pipe, HitStor disables the live updates and prints a final summary instead.

docs.title: How Deduplication Works
docs.text: HitStor uses a three-layer deduplication strategy to minimize storage consumption:

docs.title: 1. Content-Defined Chunking (FastCDC)
docs.text: Files are split into variable-length chunks using the FastCDC algorithm. Unlike fixed-size splitting, FastCDC is resilient to insertions and deletions: if you add a paragraph to the beginning of a large file, only the first few chunks change while the rest remain identical.

docs.title: 2. Chunk-Level Deduplication
docs.text: Every chunk is identified by its cryptographic hash. Before writing a chunk to the repository, HitStor checks whether a chunk with the same hash already exists. If it does, the chunk is simply referenced rather than stored again.

docs.title: 3. Pack-Level Aggregation
docs.text:
Individual chunks are grouped into pack files to reduce the number of objects in the repository and improve I/O efficiency. Each pack file contains many chunks and is accompanied by an index that maps chunk hashes to offsets within the pack.

Together these layers mean that:

  • Identical files across different snapshots are stored only once.
  • Files that differ by a small amount share most of their chunks.
  • Backups of similar machines against the same repository benefit from cross-machine deduplication.

docs.title: S3 Backend Usage
docs.text:
HitStor supports Amazon S3 (and S3-compatible services) as a backend. To back up to an S3 bucket:

hitstor init --repo s3:s3.amazonaws.com/my-bucket/hitstor-repo --password "secret"

Then run backups against the same repo URI:

hitstor backup --repo s3:s3.amazonaws.com/my-bucket/hitstor-repo \
    --password "secret" \
    /data

Configure credentials through standard AWS environment variables or the shared credentials file:

Variable Purpose AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID Access key AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Secret key AWS_DEFAULT_REGION Bucket region

For S3-compatible services (MinIO, Backblaze B2, Wasabi), point the URI to the appropriate endpoint:

hitstor init --repo s3:https://s3.us-west-001.backblazeb2.com/my-bucket/hitstor-repo \
    --password "secret"

Tip

Store your repository path and credentials in the config file or environment variables so you do not have to type them on every command. See Configuration.

docs.title: Bare-metal restore
docs.text:
Guided disaster recovery rebuilds a host that already boots and already runs a registered agent. Bare-metal restore covers the case it cannot: a machine with a blank disk, where there is no OS to install an agent onto and no partition table for the restored files to land in.

HitStor drives Relax-and-Recover (ReaR) for the parts that are not about data. ReaR builds bootable rescue media, recreates the disk layout, and reinstalls the bootloader; HitStor restores the contents.

Linux only for now

Windows bare-metal recovery (WinPE media, NTFS security descriptors, bcdboot) arrives in a later release.

docs.title: Why the media has to be built in advance
docs.text:
A rescue image embeds the host's own kernel, its drivers, and its disk layout. It can only be produced on the machine it protects, while that machine is still running — which is exactly what you no longer have when you need it.

So building recovery media is a deliberate, scheduled task, not something a backup does for you. Rebuild it whenever a host's storage layout changes: a stale image recreates the old layout.
